<h1 id="portainerce-api">PortainerCE API v2.45.3</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

The Portainer API is an HTTP API served by Portainer. It is used by the Portainer UI, and anything you can do in the UI can also be done via the HTTP API.

API examples are available in the [Portainer documentation](https://documentation.portainer.io/api/api-examples/)

You can find out more about Portainer [on our website](http://portainer.io) and get some support on [Slack](http://portainer.io/slack/).

# Authentication

Most of the API endpoints require authentication, as well as some level of authorization.
Portainer uses JSON Web Tokens to manage authentication. You must provide a token in the **Authorization** header of each request using the **Bearer** scheme.

Example:

```
Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpZCI6MSwidXNlcm5hbWUiOiJhZG1pbiIsInJvbGUiOjEsImV4cCI6MTQ5OTM3NjE1NH0.NJ6vE8FY1WG6jsRQzfMqeatJ4vh2TWAeeYfDhP71YEE
```

# Security

Each API endpoint has an associated access policy, documented in its description.

The following policies are available:

- Public access
- Authenticated access
- Restricted access
- Administrator access

### Public access

No authentication is required.

### Authenticated access

Authentication is required.

### Restricted access

Authentication is required. Additional checks may apply to verify access to the resource, and returned data may be filtered.

### Administrator access

Authentication and an administrator role are both required.

# Execute Docker requests

Portainer does not expose dedicated endpoints for managing Docker resources (create a container, remove a volume, etc).

Instead, it acts as a reverse-proxy to the Docker HTTP API, allowing you to execute Docker requests via the Portainer HTTP API.

To do so, use the `/endpoints/{id}/docker` endpoint. Note that this endpoint is not documented below due to Swagger limitations. It has a restricted access policy, so authentication is still required. Any request made to this endpoint is proxied to the Docker API of the associated environment - request and response objects are identical to those in the [Docker official documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/api).

# Private Registry

When using a private registry, include a Base64-encoded JSON string in the request header. The header parameter name is `X-Registry-Auth` and the value should encode the following structure: ‘{"registryId":\<registryId\>}’ where `<registryId>` is the ID of the registry where the repository was created.

Example encoded value:

```
eyJyZWdpc3RyeUlkIjoxfQ==
```

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/api">https://raw.githubusercontent.com/api</a>

Email: <a href="mailto:info@portainer.io">info@portainer.io</a> 
License: <a href="https://github.com/portainer/portainer/blob/HEAD/LICENSE">zlib</a>

# Authentication

* API Key (ApiKeyAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **X-API-KEY**, in: header.

* API Key (jwt)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header.

<h1 id="portainerce-api-auth">auth</h1>

Authenticate against Portainer HTTP API

## Authenticate

<a id="opIdAuthenticateUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/auth \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "Password": "mypassword",
    "Username": "admin"
  }'
```

`POST /auth`

**Access policy**: public
Use this environment(endpoint) to authenticate against Portainer using a username and password.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "Password": "mypassword",
  "Username": "admin"
}
```

<h3 id="authenticate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[auth.authenticatePayload](#schemaauth.authenticatepayload)|true|Credentials used for authentication|
|» Password|body|string|true|Password|
|» Username|body|string|true|Username|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "jwt": "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzAB"
}
```

<h3 id="authenticate-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[auth.authenticateResponse](#schemaauth.authenticateresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Credentials|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<a id="opIdLogout"></a>

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/auth/logout \

  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /auth/logout`

**Access policy**: public

<h3 id="logout-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth, jwt
</aside>

## Authenticate with OAuth

<a id="opIdValidateOAuth"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/auth/oauth/validate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "Code": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /auth/oauth/validate`

**Access policy**: public

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "Code": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="authenticate-with-oauth-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[auth.oauthPayload](#schemaauth.oauthpayload)|true|OAuth Credentials used for authentication|
|» Code|body|string|false|OAuth code returned from OAuth Provided|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "jwt": "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzAB"
}
```

<h3 id="authenticate-with-oauth-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[auth.authenticateResponse](#schemaauth.authenticateresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Credentials|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="portainerce-api-backup">backup</h1>

Manage backups

## Creates an archive with a system data snapshot that could be used to restore the system.

<a id="opIdBackup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/backup \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "Password": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /backup`

Creates an archive with a system data snapshot that could be used to restore the system.
**Access policy**: admin

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "Password": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="creates-an-archive-with-a-system-data-snapshot-that-could-be-used-to-restore-the-system-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[backup.backupPayload](#schemabackup.backuppayload)|false|An object contains the password to encrypt the backup with|
|» Password|body|string|false|none|

<h3 id="creates-an-archive-with-a-system-data-snapshot-that-could-be-used-to-restore-the-system-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth, jwt
</aside>

## Triggers a system restore using provided backup file

<a id="opIdRestore"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/restore \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "FileContent": [
      0
    ],
    "FileName": "string",
    "Password": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /restore`

Triggers a system restore using provided backup file
**Access policy**: public (requires the X-Setup-Token header on an uninitialized instance unless --no-setup-token is set)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "FileContent": [
    0
  ],
  "FileName": "string",
  "Password": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="triggers-a-system-restore-using-provided-backup-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Setup-Token|header|string|false|Setup token (required when instance is uninitialized and --no-setup-token is not set)|
|body|body|[backup.restorePayload](#schemabackup.restorepayload)|true|Restore request payload|
|» FileContent|body|[integer(int32)]|false|none|
|» FileName|body|string|false|none|
|» Password|body|string|false|none|

<h3 id="triggers-a-system-restore-using-provided-backup-file-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Access denied - invalid or missing setup token|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update a template

<a id="opIdCustomTemplateUpdate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/custom_templates/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "ComposeFilePathInRepository": "docker-compose.yml",
    "Description": "High performance web server",
    "EdgeTemplate": false,
    "FileContent": "string",
    "IsComposeFormat": false,
    "Logo": "https://portainer.io/img/logo.svg",
    "Note": "This is my <b>custom</b> template",
    "Platform": 1,
    "RepositoryAuthentication": true,
    "RepositoryPassword": "myGitPassword",
    "RepositoryReferenceName": "refs/heads/master",
    "RepositoryURL": "https://github.com/openfaas/faas",
    "RepositoryUsername": "myGitUsername",
    "SourceID": 1,
    "TLSSkipVerify": false,
    "Title": "Nginx",
    "Type": 1,
    "Variables": [
      {
        "defaultValue": "default value",
        "description": "Description",
        "label": "My Variable",
        "name": "MY_VAR"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /custom_templates/{id}`

Update a template.
**Access policy**: authenticated

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ComposeFilePathInRepository": "docker-compose.yml",
  "Description": "High performance web server",
  "EdgeTemplate": false,
  "FileContent": "string",
  "IsComposeFormat": false,
  "Logo": "https://portainer.io/img/logo.svg",
  "Note": "This is my <b>custom</b> template",
  "Platform": 1,
  "RepositoryAuthentication": true,
  "RepositoryPassword": "myGitPassword",
  "RepositoryReferenceName": "refs/heads/master",
  "RepositoryURL": "https://github.com/openfaas/faas",
  "RepositoryUsername": "myGitUsername",
  "SourceID": 1,
  "TLSSkipVerify": false,
  "Title": "Nginx",
  "Type": 1,
  "Variables": [
    {
      "defaultValue": "default value",
      "description": "Description",
      "label": "My Variable",
      "name": "MY_VAR"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Template identifier|
|body|body|[customtemplates.customTemplateUpdatePayload](#schemacustomtemplates.customtemplateupdatepayload)|true|Template details|
|» ComposeFilePathInRepository|body|string|false|Path to the Stack file inside the Git repository|
|» Description|body|string|true|Description of the template|
|» EdgeTemplate|body|boolean|false|EdgeTemplate indicates if this template purpose for Edge Stack|
|» FileContent|body|string|true|Content of stack file|
|» IsComposeFormat|body|boolean|false|IsComposeFormat indicates if the Kubernetes template is created from a Docker Compose file|
|» Logo|body|string|false|URL of the template's logo|
|» Note|body|string|false|A note that will be displayed in the UI. Supports HTML content|
|» Platform|body|integer|false|Platform associated to the template.<br>Valid values are: 1 - 'linux', 2 - 'windows'<br>Required for Docker stacks|
|» RepositoryAuthentication|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Use authentication to clone the Git repository.|
|» RepositoryPassword|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Password used in basic authentication or token used in token authentication. Required when RepositoryAuthentication is true.|
|» RepositoryReferenceName|body|string|false|Reference name of a Git repository hosting the Stack file|
|» RepositoryURL|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. URL of a Git repository hosting the Stack file.|
|» RepositoryUsername|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Username used in basic authentication. Required when RepositoryAuthentication is true.|
|» SourceID|body|integer|false|SourceID references an existing Source for git credentials/URL.<br>When set, the inline URL and authentication fields are ignored.|
|» TLSSkipVerify|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. TLSSkipVerify skips SSL verification when cloning the Git repository.|
|» Title|body|string|true|Title of the template|
|» Type|body|integer|true|Type of created stack (1 - swarm, 2 - compose, 3 - kubernetes)|
|» Variables|body|[[portainer.CustomTemplateVariableDefinition](#schemaportainer.customtemplatevariabledefinition)]|false|Definitions of variables in the stack file|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» Platform|1|
|» Platform|2|
|» Type|1|
|» Type|2|
|» Type|3|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


## Remove a template

<a id="opIdCustomTemplateDelete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/custom_templates/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /custom_templates/{id}`

Remove a template.
**Access policy**: authenticated

<h3 id="remove-a-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Template identifier|

<h3 id="remove-a-template-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Access denied to resource|None|

<h3 id="create-a-custom-template-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[customtemplates.customTemplateFromGitRepositoryPayload](#schemacustomtemplates.customtemplatefromgitrepositorypayload)|true|Required when using method=repository|
|» ComposeFilePathInRepository|body|string|false|Path to the Stack file inside the Git repository|
|» Description|body|string|true|Description of the template|
|» EdgeTemplate|body|boolean|false|EdgeTemplate indicates if this template purpose for Edge Stack|
|» IsComposeFormat|body|boolean|false|IsComposeFormat indicates if the Kubernetes template is created from a Docker Compose file|
|» Logo|body|string|false|URL of the template's logo|
|» Note|body|string|false|A note that will be displayed in the UI. Supports HTML content|
|» Platform|body|integer|false|Platform associated to the template.<br>Valid values are: 1 - 'linux', 2 - 'windows'<br>Required for Docker stacks|
|» RepositoryAuthentication|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Use basic authentication to clone the Git repository.|
|» RepositoryPassword|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Password used in basic authentication. Required when RepositoryAuthentication is true.|
|» RepositoryReferenceName|body|string|false|Reference name of a Git repository hosting the Stack file|
|» RepositoryURL|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. URL of a Git repository hosting the Stack file.|
|» RepositoryUsername|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Username used in basic authentication. Required when RepositoryAuthentication is true.|
|» SourceID|body|integer|true|SourceID references an existing Source for git credentials/URL.<br>When set, the inline URL and authentication fields are ignored.|
|» TLSSkipVerify|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. TLSSkipVerify skips SSL verification when cloning the Git repository.|
|» Title|body|string|true|Title of the template|
|» Type|body|integer|true|Type of created stack:<br>* 1 - swarm<br>* 2 - compose<br>* 3 - kubernetes|
|» Variables|body|[[portainer.CustomTemplateVariableDefinition](#schemaportainer.customtemplatevariabledefinition)]|false|Definitions of variables in the stack file|

|---|---|
|» Platform|1|

|» Type|1|
|» Type|2|

## Create an EdgeStack from a git repository

<a id="opIdEdgeStackCreateRepository"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/edge_stacks/create/repository \

    "EdgeGroups": [

    ],

    "RepositoryUsername": "myGitUsername",
    "SourceID": 1,
    "TLSSkipVerify": false,
    "UseManifestNamespaces": true
  }'
```

<h3 id="create-an-edgestack-from-a-git-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dryrun|query|string|false|if true, will not create an edge stack, but just will check the settings and return a non-persisted edge stack object|
|body|body|[edgestacks.edgeStackFromGitRepositoryPayload](#schemaedgestacks.edgestackfromgitrepositorypayload)|true|stack config|
|» DeploymentType|body|integer|false|Deployment type to deploy this stack<br>Valid values are: 0 - 'compose', 1 - 'kubernetes'<br>compose is enabled only for docker environments<br>kubernetes is enabled only for kubernetes environments|
|» EdgeGroups|body|[integer]|true|List of identifiers of EdgeGroups|
|» FilePathInRepository|body|string|false|Path to the Stack file inside the Git repository|
|» Name|body|string|true|Name of the stack<br>Max length: 255<br>Name must only contains lowercase characters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores<br>Name must start with a lowercase character or number<br>Example: stack-name or stack_123 or stackName|
|» Registries|body|[integer]|false|List of Registries to use for this stack|
|» RepositoryAuthentication|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: Use SourceID instead. Use basic authentication to clone the Git repository.|
|» RepositoryPassword|body|string|false|Deprecated: Use SourceID instead. Password used in basic authentication.|
|» RepositoryReferenceName|body|string|false|Reference name of a Git repository hosting the Stack file|
|» RepositoryURL|body|string|false|Deprecated: Use SourceID instead. URL of a Git repository hosting the Stack file.|
|» RepositoryUsername|body|string|false|Deprecated: Use SourceID instead. Username used in basic authentication.|
|» SourceID|body|integer|false|SourceID references an existing Source for git credentials/URL.<br>When set, the inline URL and authentication fields are ignored.|
|» TLSSkipVerify|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: Use SourceID instead. TLSSkipVerify skips SSL verification when cloning the Git repository.|
|» UseManifestNamespaces|body|boolean|false|Uses the manifest's namespaces instead of the default one|

<h1 id="portainerce-api-endpoints">endpoints</h1>

Manage environments

## List environments(endpoints)

<a id="opIdEndpointList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/endpoints \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /endpoints`

List all environments(endpoints) based on the current user authorizations. Will
return all environments(endpoints) if using an administrator or team leader account otherwise it will
only return authorized environments(endpoints).
**Access policy**: restricted

<h3 id="list-environmentsendpoints-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start|query|integer|false|Start searching from|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limit results to this value|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort results by this value|
|order|query|string|false|Order sorted results by desc/asc|
|search|query|string|false|Search query|
|groupIds|query|[integer]|false|List environments(endpoints) of these groups|
|status|query|[integer]|false|List environments(endpoints) by this status|
|types|query|[integer]|false|List environments(endpoints) of this type|
|platformTypes|query|[integer]|false|Filter environments by platform type|
|outdated|query|boolean|false|If true, return only environments with an outdated agent|
|excludeGroupIds|query|[integer]|false|Exclude environments of these groups|
|tagIds|query|[integer]|false|search environments(endpoints) with these tags (depends on tagsPartialMatch)|
|tagsPartialMatch|query|boolean|false|If true, will return environment(endpoint) which has one of tagIds, if false (or missing) will return only environments(endpoints) that has all the tags|
|endpointIds|query|[integer]|false|will return only these environments(endpoints)|
|excludeIds|query|[integer]|false|will exclude these environments(endpoints)|
|agentVersions|query|[string]|false|will return only environments with on of these agent versions|
|edgeAsync|query|boolean|false|if exists true show only edge async agents, false show only standard edge agents. if missing, will show both types (relevant only for edge agents)|
|edgeDeviceUntrusted|query|boolean|false|if true, show only untrusted edge agents, if false show only trusted edge agents (relevant only for edge agents)|
|edgeCheckInPassedSeconds|query|number|false|if bigger then zero, show only edge agents that checked-in in the last provided seconds (relevant only for edge agents)|
|excludeSnapshots|query|boolean|false|if true, the snapshot data won't be retrieved|
|name|query|string|false|will return only environments(endpoints) with this name|
|edgeStackId|query|integer|false|will return the environments of the specified edge stack|
|edgeStackStatus|query|integer|false|only applied when edgeStackId exists. Filter the returned environments based on their deployment status in the stack (not the environment status!)|
|edgeGroupIds|query|[integer]|false|List environments(endpoints) of these edge groups|
|excludeEdgeGroupIds|query|[integer]|false|Exclude environments(endpoints) of these edge groups|

## Create a new environment(endpoint)

<a id="opIdEndpointCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/endpoints \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'Name=string' \
  -F 'EndpointCreationType=0' \
  -F 'ContainerEngine=string' \
  -F 'URL=string' \
  -F 'PublicURL=string' \
  -F 'GroupID=0' \
  -F 'TLS=true' \
  -F 'TLSSkipVerify=true' \
  -F 'TLSSkipClientVerify=true' \
  -F 'TLSCACertFile=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'TLSCertFile=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'TLSKeyFile=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'AzureApplicationID=string' \
  -F 'AzureTenantID=string' \
  -F 'AzureAuthenticationKey=string' \
  -F 'TagIds=string' \
  -F 'EdgeCheckinInterval=0' \
  -F 'EdgeTunnelServerAddress=string' \
  -F 'Gpus=string'
```

`POST /endpoints`

Create a new environment(endpoint) that will be used to manage an environment(endpoint).
**Access policy**: administrator

> Body parameter

```yaml
Name: string
EndpointCreationType: 0
ContainerEngine: string
URL: string
PublicURL: string
GroupID: 0
TLS: true
TLSSkipVerify: true
TLSSkipClientVerify: true
TLSCACertFile: string
TLSCertFile: string
TLSKeyFile: string
AzureApplicationID: string
AzureTenantID: string
AzureAuthenticationKey: string
TagIds: string
EdgeCheckinInterval: 0
EdgeTunnelServerAddress: string
Gpus: string
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-environmentendpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» Name|body|string|true|Name that will be used to identify this environment(endpoint) (example: my-environment)|
|» EndpointCreationType|body|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) type. Value must be one of: 1 (Local Docker environment), 2 (Agent environment), 3 (Azure environment), 4 (Edge agent environment) or 5 (Local Kubernetes Environment)|
|» ContainerEngine|body|string|false|Container engine used by the environment(endpoint). Value must be one of: 'docker' or 'podman'|
|» URL|body|string|false|URL or IP address of a Docker host (example: docker.mydomain.tld:2375). Defaults to local if not specified (Linux: /var/run/docker.sock, Windows: //./pipe/docker_engine). Cannot be empty if EndpointCreationType is set to 4 (Edge agent environment)|
|» PublicURL|body|string|false|URL or IP address where exposed containers will be reachable. Defaults to URL if not specified (example: docker.mydomain.tld:2375)|
|» GroupID|body|integer|false|Environment(Endpoint) group identifier. If not specified will default to 1 (unassigned).|
|» TLS|body|boolean|false|Require TLS to connect against this environment(endpoint). Must be true if EndpointCreationType is set to 2 (Agent environment)|
|» TLSSkipVerify|body|boolean|false|Skip server verification when using TLS. Must be true if EndpointCreationType is set to 2 (Agent environment)|
|» TLSSkipClientVerify|body|boolean|false|Skip client verification when using TLS. Must be true if EndpointCreationType is set to 2 (Agent environment)|
|» TLSCACertFile|body|string(binary)|false|TLS CA certificate file|
|» TLSCertFile|body|string(binary)|false|TLS client certificate file|
|» TLSKeyFile|body|string(binary)|false|TLS client key file|
|» AzureApplicationID|body|string|false|Azure application ID. Required if environment(endpoint) type is set to 3|
|» AzureTenantID|body|string|false|Azure tenant ID. Required if environment(endpoint) type is set to 3|
|» AzureAuthenticationKey|body|string|false|Azure authentication key. Required if environment(endpoint) type is set to 3|
|» TagIds|body|string|false|JSON-parsable array of tag identifiers to which this environment(endpoint) is associated|
|» EdgeCheckinInterval|body|integer|false|The check in interval for edge agent (in seconds)|
|» EdgeTunnelServerAddress|body|string|false|URL or IP address that will be used to establish a reverse tunnel|
|» Gpus|body|string|false|List of GPUs - json stringified array of {name, value} structs|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» EndpointCreationType|0|
|» EndpointCreationType|1|
|» EndpointCreationType|2|
|» EndpointCreationType|3|
|» EndpointCreationType|4|
|» EndpointCreationType|5|

## Remove multiple environments

<a id="opIdEndpointDeleteBatchDeprecated"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/endpoints \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "endpoints": [
      {
        "deleteCluster": true,
        "id": 0
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /endpoints`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Deprecated: use the `POST` endpoint instead.
Remove multiple environments and optionally clean-up associated resources.
**Access policy**: Administrator only.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "endpoints": [
    {
      "deleteCluster": true,
      "id": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-multiple-environments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[endpoints.endpointDeleteBatchPayload](#schemaendpoints.endpointdeletebatchpayload)|true|List of environments to delete, with optional deleteCluster flag to clean-up associated resources (cloud environments only)|
|» endpoints|body|[[endpoints.endpointDeleteRequest](#schemaendpoints.endpointdeleterequest)]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 207 Response

```json
{
  "deleted": [
    0
  ],
  "errors": [
    0
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-multiple-environments-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Environment(s) successfully deleted.|None|
|207|Multi-Status|Partial success. Some environments were deleted successfully, while others failed.|[endpoints.endpointDeleteBatchPartialResponse](#schemaendpoints.endpointdeletebatchpartialresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Unauthorized access or operation not allowed.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to delete the specified environments.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

<h3 id="update-an-environmentendpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|body|body|[endpoints.endpointUpdatePayload](#schemaendpoints.endpointupdatepayload)|true|Environment(Endpoint) details|
|» AzureApplicationID|body|string|false|Azure application ID|
|» AzureAuthenticationKey|body|string|false|Azure authentication key|
|» AzureTenantID|body|string|false|Azure tenant ID|
|» EdgeCheckinInterval|body|integer|false|The check in interval for edge agent (in seconds)|
|» Gpus|body|[[portainer.Pair](#schemaportainer.pair)]|false|GPUs information|
|» GroupID|body|integer|false|Group identifier|
|» Kubernetes|body|object|false|Associated Kubernetes data|
|» » Configuration|body|[portainer.KubernetesConfiguration](#schemaportainer.kubernetesconfiguration)|true|none|
|» » Flags|body|[portainer.KubernetesFlags](#schemaportainer.kubernetesflags)|true|none|
|» » Snapshots|body|[[portainer.KubernetesSnapshot](#schemaportainer.kubernetessnapshot)]|false|none|
|» Name|body|string|false|Name that will be used to identify this environment(endpoint)|
|» PublicURL|body|string|false|URL or IP address where exposed containers will be reachable.\<br>Defaults to URL if not specified|
|» Status|body|integer|false|The status of the environment(endpoint) (1 - up, 2 - down)|
|» TLS|body|boolean|false|Require TLS to connect against this environment(endpoint)|
|» TLSSkipClientVerify|body|boolean|false|Skip client verification when using TLS|
|» TLSSkipVerify|body|boolean|false|Skip server verification when using TLS|
|» TagIDs|body|[integer]|false|List of tag identifiers to which this environment(endpoint) is associated|
|» TeamAccessPolicies|body|[portainer.TeamAccessPolicies](#schemaportainer.teamaccesspolicies)|false|none|
|» URL|body|string|false|URL or IP address of a Docker host|
|» UserAccessPolicies|body|[portainer.UserAccessPolicies](#schemaportainer.useraccesspolicies)|false|none|

## Remove an environment

<a id="opIdEndpointDelete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/endpoints/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /endpoints/{id}`

Remove the environment associated to the specified identifier and optionally clean-up associated resources.
**Access policy**: Administrator only.

<h3 id="remove-an-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|

<h3 id="remove-an-environment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Environment successfully deleted.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Unauthorized access or operation not allowed.|None|
|404|Not Found|Unable to find the environment with the specified identifier inside the database.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to delete the environment.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

## Upload a file under a specific path on the file system of an environment (endpoint)

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/endpoints/0/docker/v2/browse/put \
  -X POST \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'Path=string' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /endpoints/{id}/docker/v2/browse/put`

Use this environment(endpoint) to upload TLS files.
**Access policy**: administrator

> Body parameter

```yaml
Path: string
file: string
```

<h3 id="upload-a-file-under-a-specific-path-on-the-file-system-of-an-environment-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|volumeID|query|string|false|Optional volume identifier to upload the file|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» Path|body|string|true|The destination path to upload the file to|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The file to upload|

## preview the content of target file in the git repository

<a id="opIdGitOperationRepoFilePreview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/gitops/repo/file/preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "password": "myGitPassword",
    "reference": "refs/heads/master",
    "repository": "https://github.com/openfaas/faas",
    "sourceID": 1,
    "targetFile": "docker-compose.yml",
    "tlsSkipVerify": false,
    "username": "myGitUsername"
  }'
```

`POST /gitops/repo/file/preview`

Retrieve the compose file content based on git repository configuration
**Access policy**: authenticated

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "password": "myGitPassword",
  "reference": "refs/heads/master",
  "repository": "https://github.com/openfaas/faas",
  "sourceID": 1,
  "targetFile": "docker-compose.yml",
  "tlsSkipVerify": false,
  "username": "myGitUsername"
}
```

<h3 id="preview-the-content-of-target-file-in-the-git-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[gitops.repositoryFilePreviewPayload](#schemagitops.repositoryfilepreviewpayload)|true|Template details|
|» password|body|string|false|Password for git authentication.<br>Deprecated: use SourceID instead|
|» reference|body|string|false|none|
|» repository|body|string|false|URL of a Git repository to preview.<br>Deprecated: use SourceID instead|
|» sourceID|body|integer|false|SourceID resolves URL and auth from the stored Source record.<br>When set, the inline Repository/Username/Password/TLSSkipVerify fields are ignored.|
|» targetFile|body|string|false|Path to file whose content will be read|
|» tlsSkipVerify|body|boolean|false|TLSSkipVerify skips SSL verification when cloning the Git repository.<br>Deprecated: use SourceID instead|
|» username|body|string|false|Username for git authentication.<br>Deprecated: use SourceID instead|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "FileContent": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="preview-the-content-of-target-file-in-the-git-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|404|Not Found|Source not found|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error|None|

|start|query|integer|false|Pagination start index|
|limit|query|integer|false|Pagination limit (0 = unlimited)|
|status|query|string|false|Filter by status: healthy \| syncing \| error \| paused \| unknown|
|type|query|string|false|Filter by source type: git \| oci \| helm|

|Parameter|Value|

## Test the connection of a stored source

<a id="opIdGitOpsSourcesTestById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/gitops/sources/0/test \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "authentication": {
      "password": "string",
      "username": "string"
    },
    "interval": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "tlsSkipVerify": true,
    "url": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /gitops/sources/{id}/test`

Tests connectivity for a GitOps source, applying optional overrides to the stored configuration.
The test ignores the name and interval fields. To send any other field, the user must be the owner of the source or an administrator. Other users can only test the stored settings.
**Access policy**: authenticated

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "authentication": {
    "password": "string",
    "username": "string"
  },
  "interval": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "tlsSkipVerify": true,
  "url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="test-the-connection-of-a-stored-source-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Source identifier|
|body|body|[sources.GitSourceUpdatePayload](#schemasources.gitsourceupdatepayload)|false|Optional changes to the stored settings, used only for this test. A field that is not sent keeps its stored value. Fields other than name and interval need write access to the source|
|» authentication|body|[sources.GitAuthenticationUpdatePayload](#schemasources.gitauthenticationupdatepayload)|false|none|
|» interval|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» tlsSkipVerify|body|boolean|false|none|
|» url|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "success": true
}
```

<h3 id="test-the-connection-of-a-stored-source-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Connection test result|[sources.ConnectionTestResult](#schemasources.connectiontestresult)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload|None|
|403|Forbidden|Access denied, or the request changes settings and the user has no write access to the source|None|
|404|Not Found|Source not found|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth, jwt
</aside>

## Rollback a helm release

<a id="opIdHelmRollback"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/endpoints/0/kubernetes/helm/string/rollback \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /endpoints/{id}/kubernetes/helm/{release}/rollback`

Rollback a helm release to a previous revision
**Access policy**: authenticated

<h3 id="rollback-a-helm-release-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|release|path|string|true|Helm release name|
|namespace|query|string|false|specify an optional namespace|
|revision|query|integer|false|specify the revision to rollback to (defaults to previous revision if not specified)|
|wait|query|boolean|false|wait for resources to be ready (default: false)|
|waitForJobs|query|boolean|false|wait for jobs to complete before marking the release as successful (default: false)|
|recreate|query|boolean|false|performs pods restart for the resource if applicable (default: true)|
|force|query|boolean|false|force resource update through delete/recreate if needed (default: false)|
|timeout|query|integer|false|time to wait for any individual Kubernetes operation in seconds (default: 300)|

```json
  ],
```
```bash
  "property2": [

  ]
```
```json
}
```

## Validate Kubernetes manifests without applying them

<a id="opIdDryRunKubernetesManifests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/manifests/dry_run \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "manifests": [
      "apiVersion: v1\nkind: ConfigMap\nmetadata:\n  name: app-config"
    ],
    "namespace": "default"
  }'
```

`POST /kubernetes/{id}/manifests/dry_run`

Validate Kubernetes manifests against the cluster with a server-side dry-run apply, without persisting anything.
Each resource is reported on its own, so a rejected resource does not hide the outcome of the others.
The dry-run runs with the permissions of the requesting user, so it also surfaces missing permissions.
A resource living in a namespace created by another manifest of the same request is reported as failed, because the dry-run never persists that namespace.
**Access policy**: authenticated

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "manifests": [
    "apiVersion: v1\nkind: ConfigMap\nmetadata:\n  name: app-config"
  ],
  "namespace": "default"
}
```

<h3 id="validate-kubernetes-manifests-without-applying-them-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|body|body|[kubernetes.manifestDryRunPayload](#schemakubernetes.manifestdryrunpayload)|true|The manifests to validate|
|» manifests|body|[string]|false|The manifests to validate. Each entry may hold several YAML documents separated by "---".|
|» namespace|body|string|false|The namespace applied to namespaced resources that do not declare one. A resource declaring a different namespace is rejected.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "documentIndex": 0,
      "kind": "ConfigMap",
      "message": "string",
      "name": "app-config",
      "namespace": "default",
      "status": "pass"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="validate-kubernetes-manifests-without-applying-them-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[kubernetes.manifestDryRunResponse](#schemakubernetes.manifestdryrunresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Unable to find an environment with the specified identifier.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to validate the manifests.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

<h3 id="get-kubernetes-deployments-within-a-namespace-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[kubernetes.KubernetesDeploymentListResponse](#schemakubernetes.kubernetesdeploymentlistresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to retrieve the deployments within the specified namespace.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

`POST /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/deployments`

Create a deployment in the given namespace. The namespace comes from the
route, and the payload models the fields the deployment forms drive.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="create-a-kubernetes-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|body|body|[kubernetes.K8sDeploymentWriteRequest](#schemakubernetes.k8sdeploymentwriterequest)|true|Deployment definition|
|» annotations|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» labels|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» pod|body|[kubernetes.K8sPodTemplate](#schemakubernetes.k8spodtemplate)|false|none|
|» replicas|body|integer|false|none|
|» selector|body|object|false|Selector matches the pods this deployment owns. It is immutable once the<br>deployment exists, so it is only read on create.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

<h3 id="create-a-kubernetes-deployment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[kubernetes.KubernetesDeploymentResponse](#schemakubernetes.kubernetesdeploymentresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|409|Conflict|A deployment with the same name already exists in the namespace.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to create the deployment.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

## Get a Kubernetes deployment

<a id="opIdgetKubernetesDeployment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/deployments/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/deployments/{name}`

Get a Kubernetes deployment in the given namespace. The response is
trimmed of server-managed and heavy fields (managed fields,
last-applied-config annotation) while preserving the full pod template,
spec and resourceVersion so an edit form can be reconstructed from the
live cluster and the workload subsequently updated.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="get-a-kubernetes-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|name|path|string|true|Deployment name|

|200|OK|Success|[kubernetes.KubernetesDeploymentResponse](#schemakubernetes.kubernetesdeploymentresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|

|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to retrieve the deployment.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

`PUT /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/deployments/{name}`

Update a deployment in the given namespace. The payload is merged onto the
live deployment: fields it does not model, such as the update strategy or
the pod affinity rules, are preserved, and a field left out leaves the live
value untouched. The selector is immutable and is ignored.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="update-a-kubernetes-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|name|path|string|true|Deployment name|
|body|body|[kubernetes.K8sDeploymentWriteRequest](#schemakubernetes.k8sdeploymentwriterequest)|true|Deployment definition|
|» annotations|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» labels|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» pod|body|[kubernetes.K8sPodTemplate](#schemakubernetes.k8spodtemplate)|false|none|
|» replicas|body|integer|false|none|
|» selector|body|object|false|Selector matches the pods this deployment owns. It is immutable once the<br>deployment exists, so it is only read on create.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

<h3 id="update-a-kubernetes-deployment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[kubernetes.KubernetesDeploymentResponse](#schemakubernetes.kubernetesdeploymentresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields, fields not meeting validation criteria, or a payload name that does not match the route.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Unable to find the deployment to update.|None|
|409|Conflict|The deployment was modified concurrently.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to update the deployment.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

## Delete a Kubernetes deployment

<a id="opIdDeleteKubernetesDeployment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/deployments/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/deployments/{name}`

Delete a deployment in the given namespace. The replica sets and pods it
owns are garbage collected by the cluster.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="delete-a-kubernetes-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|name|path|string|true|Deployment name|

<h3 id="delete-a-kubernetes-deployment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Unable to find the deployment to delete.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to delete the deployment.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

## Annotate a Kubernetes deployment

<a id="opIdPatchKubernetesDeployment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/deployments/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "annotations": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "podAnnotations": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/deployments/{name}`

Add or overwrite annotations on a deployment and on the pods it creates.
Annotations the payload does not name are kept. Changing a pod annotation
rolls the workload, which is how a rollout restart is triggered.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "annotations": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "podAnnotations": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="annotate-a-kubernetes-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|name|path|string|true|Deployment name|
|body|body|[kubernetes.K8sDeploymentPatchRequest](#schemakubernetes.k8sdeploymentpatchrequest)|true|Annotations to apply|
|» annotations|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» podAnnotations|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

<h3 id="annotate-a-kubernetes-deployment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[kubernetes.KubernetesDeploymentResponse](#schemakubernetes.kubernetesdeploymentresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Unable to find the deployment to annotate.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to annotate the deployment.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

## Roll a Kubernetes deployment back

<a id="opIdRollbackKubernetesDeployment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/deployments/string/rollback \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "revision": 0
  }'
```

`POST /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/deployments/{name}/rollback`

Roll a deployment back to an earlier revision by replaying the pod template
the corresponding replica set recorded. A revision of 0, or an omitted one,
selects the revision immediately before the current.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revision": 0
}
```

<h3 id="roll-a-kubernetes-deployment-back-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|name|path|string|true|Deployment name|
|body|body|[kubernetes.K8sDeploymentRollbackRequest](#schemakubernetes.k8sdeploymentrollbackrequest)|true|Revision to roll back to|
|» revision|body|integer|false|none|

<h3 id="roll-a-kubernetes-deployment-back-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[kubernetes.KubernetesDeploymentResponse](#schemakubernetes.kubernetesdeploymentresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Unable to find the deployment, or the requested revision is not part of its rollout history.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to roll the deployment back.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

## Scale a Kubernetes deployment

<a id="opIdScaleKubernetesDeployment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/deployments/string/scale \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "replicas": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/deployments/{name}/scale`

Set the desired replica count of a deployment in the given namespace.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "replicas": 0
}
```

<h3 id="scale-a-kubernetes-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|name|path|string|true|Deployment name|
|body|body|[kubernetes.K8sDeploymentScaleRequest](#schemakubernetes.k8sdeploymentscalerequest)|true|Desired replica count|
|» replicas|body|integer|false|none|

## Gets kubernetes events for namespace

<a id="opIdgetKubernetesEventsForNamespace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/events`

Get events by optional query param resourceId for a given namespace.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="gets-kubernetes-events-for-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|The namespace name the events are associated to|
|resourceId|query|string|false|The resource id of the involved kubernetes object|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "count": 0,
    "eventTime": "string",
    "firstTimestamp": "string",
    "involvedObject": {
      "kind": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "namespace": "string",
      "uid": "string"
    },
    "kind": "string",
    "lastTimestamp": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "namespace": "string",
    "reason": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "uid": "string"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="gets-kubernetes-events-for-namespace-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to retrieve the events within the specified namespace.|None|

<h3 id="gets-kubernetes-events-for-namespace-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[kubernetes.K8sEvent](#schemakubernetes.k8sevent)]|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt

## Get Kubernetes pods within a namespace

<a id="opIdgetKubernetesPodsForNamespace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/pods \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/pods`

Get the list of Kubernetes pods in the given namespace.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="get-kubernetes-pods-within-a-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|labelSelector|query|string|false|Kubernetes label selector to filter the pods (e.g. app=nginx)|
|fieldSelector|query|string|false|Kubernetes field selector to filter the pods (e.g. status.phase=Running)|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to retrieve the pods within the specified namespace.|None|

<aside class="warning">

ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

## Delete a kubernetes pod

<a id="opIdDeleteKubernetesPod"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/pods/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/pods/{name}`

Delete a single Kubernetes pod in the given namespace. The owning
controller (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, ...) is responsible
for recreating the pod. For naked pods the pod is removed permanently.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="delete-a-kubernetes-pod-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|name|path|string|true|Pod name|

<h3 id="delete-a-kubernetes-pod-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Unable to find an environment with the specified identifier or unable to find the specified pod.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to delete the pod.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

## Get logs for a Kubernetes pod

<a id="opIdgetKubernetesPodLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/pods/string/log \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/pods/{name}/log`

Stream the logs for a pod in the given namespace as text/plain. When
follow is set the response stays open and emits new log lines until the
client disconnects. When the pod has more than one container, the
container query parameter is required.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="get-logs-for-a-kubernetes-pod-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|name|path|string|true|Pod name|
|container|query|string|false|Container name (required when the pod has multiple containers)|
|tailLines|query|integer|false|Number of lines from the end of the logs to return|
|sinceSeconds|query|integer|false|Only return logs newer than this many seconds|
|timestamps|query|boolean|false|Prefix each log line with an RFC3339 timestamp|
|previous|query|boolean|false|Return the logs of the previous terminated container instance|
|follow|query|boolean|false|Stream new log lines as they are produced until the client disconnects|

<h3 id="get-logs-for-a-kubernetes-pod-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to retrieve the pod logs.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

## Restart all containers in a Kubernetes pod

<a id="opIdRestartKubernetesPod"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/pods/string/restart \
  -X POST \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/pods/{name}/restart`

Restart all containers in a single Kubernetes pod in place using
the Kubernetes 1.35 alpha pod-restart subresource. The pod itself
is preserved. Requires the cluster to expose the corresponding
subresource (and the matching feature gate to be enabled).
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="restart-all-containers-in-a-kubernetes-pod-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|name|path|string|true|Pod name|

<h3 id="restart-all-containers-in-a-kubernetes-pod-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Unable to find an environment, the specified pod, or the cluster does not expose the pod-restart subresource (Kubernetes <1.35 or feature gate disabled).|None|
|405|Method Not Allowed|The cluster does not support the pod-restart subresource (Kubernetes <1.35 or feature gate disabled).|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to restart the pod.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

## Get Kubernetes replica sets within a namespace

<a id="opIdgetKubernetesReplicaSets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/replicasets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/replicasets`

Get the list of Kubernetes replica sets in the given namespace, optionally
restricted to those owned by a given deployment. This backs the deployment
revisions view. The response uses the Kubernetes list shape ({items: [...]}).
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="get-kubernetes-replica-sets-within-a-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace|
|deployment|query|string|false|Only return replica sets owned by this deployment|
|labelSelector|query|string|false|Kubernetes label selector to filter the replica sets|
|fieldSelector|query|string|false|Kubernetes field selector to filter the replica sets|

`POST /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/secrets`

strings and encoded server-side. The response carries the created

Update a Secret in the given namespace. A nil field leaves the live value
untouched, so an empty map clears it, and the secret type cannot be
changed. The response carries the updated Secret's metadata only.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "Annotations": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "Data": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "Labels": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "Name": "string",
  "SecretType": "string"
}
```

|body|body|[kubernetes.K8sSecretWriteRequest](#schemakubernetes.k8ssecretwriterequest)|true|Secret definition|
|» Annotations|body|object|false|none|

## Toggle the system state for a namespace

<a id="opIdKubernetesNamespacesToggleSystem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/system \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "System": true
  }'
```

`PUT /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/system`

Toggle the system state for a namespace
**Access policy**: Administrator or environment administrator.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "System": true
}
```

<h3 id="toggle-the-system-state-for-a-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace name|
|body|body|[kubernetes.namespacesToggleSystemPayload](#schemakubernetes.namespacestogglesystempayload)|true|Update details|
|» System|body|boolean|false|Toggle the system state of this namespace to true or false|

<h3 id="toggle-the-system-state-for-a-namespace-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Unable to find an environment with the specified identifier or unable to find the namespace to update.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to update the system state of the namespace.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

## Get Kubernetes volumes within a namespace in the given Portainer environment

<a id="opIdGetKubernetesVolumesInNamespace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/string/volumes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/{namespace}/volumes`

Get a list of kubernetes volumes within the specified namespace in the given environment (Endpoint). The Endpoint ID must be a valid Portainer environment identifier.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="get-kubernetes-volumes-within-a-namespace-in-the-given-portainer-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment identifier|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace identifier|
|withApplications|query|boolean|false|When set to True, include the applications that are using the volumes. It is set to false by default|

## Get the total number of kubernetes namespaces within the given Portainer environment.

<a id="opIdGetKubernetesNamespacesCount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/namespaces/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /kubernetes/{id}/namespaces/count`

Get the total number of kubernetes namespaces within the given environment, including the system namespaces. The total count depends on the user's role and permissions.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="get-the-total-number-of-kubernetes-namespaces-within-the-given-portainer-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment identifier|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
0
```

<h3 id="get-the-total-number-of-kubernetes-namespaces-within-the-given-portainer-environment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

## Drain a Kubernetes node

<a id="opIddrainNode"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/nodes/string/drain \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "DeleteEmptyDirData": true,
    "DisableEviction": false,
    "Force": false,
    "GracePeriodSeconds": -1,
    "IgnoreDaemonSets": true,
    "TimeoutSeconds": 60
  }'
```

`POST /kubernetes/{id}/nodes/{name}/drain`

Drain a Kubernetes node by safely evicting all pods from the node, preparing it for maintenance or removal
**Access policy**: authenticated

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "DeleteEmptyDirData": true,
  "DisableEviction": false,
  "Force": false,
  "GracePeriodSeconds": -1,
  "IgnoreDaemonSets": true,
  "TimeoutSeconds": 60
}
```

<h3 id="drain-a-kubernetes-node-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the node to drain|
|body|body|[kubernetes.drainNodePayload](#schemakubernetes.drainnodepayload)|false|Drain options, matching kubectl drain flags. Defaults are applied to any omitted field.|
|» DeleteEmptyDirData|body|boolean|false|DeleteEmptyDirData allows eviction of pods using emptyDir volumes, whose data is lost once the pod is deleted.|
|» DisableEviction|body|boolean|false|DisableEviction forces the use of direct pod deletion instead of the eviction API, ignoring any configured PodDisruptionBudgets.|
|» Force|body|boolean|false|Force allows deletion of standalone pods not managed by a controller.|
|» GracePeriodSeconds|body|integer|false|GracePeriodSeconds overrides each pod's termination grace period. -1 uses the pod's own grace period.|
|» IgnoreDaemonSets|body|boolean|false|IgnoreDaemonSets skips DaemonSet-managed pods, which would otherwise block the drain.|
|» TimeoutSeconds|body|integer|false|TimeoutSeconds is the overall time to wait for the drain to complete. Defaults to 60 when omitted.|

<h3 id="drain-a-kubernetes-node-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Unable to find an environment with the specified identifier or unable to find the specified node.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to drain node.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

|200|OK|Success|[kubernetes.K8sPersistentVolume](#schemakubernetes.k8spersistentvolume)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Unauthorized access or operation not allowed.|None|
|404|Not Found|PersistentVolume not found.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to retrieve the persistent volume.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

```bash
    "string"
  ]'
```

`POST /kubernetes/{id}/persistent_volumes/delete`

```json
[
  "string"
```

## Update reclaim policy of a PersistentVolume

<a id="opIdUpdateKubernetesPersistentVolumeReclaimPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/0/persistent_volumes/reclaim_policy \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "reclaimPolicy": "Recycle"
  }'
```

`PUT /kubernetes/{id}/persistent_volumes/reclaim_policy`

Update the reclaim policy of a PersistentVolume.
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "reclaimPolicy": "Recycle"
}
```

<h3 id="update-reclaim-policy-of-a-persistentvolume-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Environment identifier|
|body|body|[kubernetes.K8sPVReclaimPolicyRequest](#schemakubernetes.k8spvreclaimpolicyrequest)|true|Reclaim policy update request|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» reclaimPolicy|body|[v1.PersistentVolumeReclaimPolicy](#schemav1.persistentvolumereclaimpolicy)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» reclaimPolicy|Recycle|
|» reclaimPolicy|Delete|
|» reclaimPolicy|Retain|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Unauthorized access or operation not allowed.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to update reclaim policy.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>
