## Generate a kubeconfig file

<a id="opIdGetKubernetesConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/kubernetes/config \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /kubernetes/config`

Generate a kubeconfig file that allows a client to communicate with the Kubernetes API server
**Access policy**: Authenticated user.

<h3 id="generate-a-kubeconfig-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|[integer]|false|will include only these environments(endpoints)|
|excludeIds|query|[integer]|false|will exclude these environments(endpoints)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="generate-a-kubeconfig-file-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request payload, such as missing required fields or fields not meeting validation criteria.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized access - the user is not authenticated or does not have the necessary permissions. Ensure that you have provided a valid API key or JWT token, and that you have the required permissions.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Permission denied - the user is authenticated but does not have the necessary permissions to access the requested resource or perform the specified operation. Check your user roles and permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Unable to find an environment with the specified identifier.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error occurred while attempting to generate the kubeconfig file.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth & jwt
</aside>

<h1 id="portainerce-api-ldap">ldap</h1>

Manage LDAP settings

## Test LDAP connectivity

<a id="opIdLDAPCheck"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/ldap/check \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "LDAPSettings": {
      "AnonymousMode": true,
      "AutoCreateUsers": true,
      "GroupSearchSettings": [
        {
          "GroupAttribute": "member",
          "GroupBaseDN": "dc=ldap,dc=domain,dc=tld",
          "GroupFilter": "(objectClass=account"
        }
      ],
      "Password": "readonly-password",
      "ReaderDN": "cn=readonly-account,dc=ldap,dc=domain,dc=tld",
      "SearchSettings": [
        {
          "BaseDN": "dc=ldap,dc=domain,dc=tld",
          "Filter": "(objectClass=account)",
          "UserNameAttribute": "uid"
        }
      ],
      "StartTLS": true,
      "TLSConfig": {
        "TLS": true,
        "TLSCACert": "/data/tls/ca.pem",
        "TLSCert": "/data/tls/cert.pem",
        "TLSKey": "/data/tls/key.pem",
        "TLSSkipVerify": false
      },
      "URL": "myldap.domain.tld:389"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /ldap/check`

Test LDAP connectivity using LDAP details
**Access policy**: administrator

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "LDAPSettings": {
    "AnonymousMode": true,
    "AutoCreateUsers": true,
    "GroupSearchSettings": [
      {
        "GroupAttribute": "member",
        "GroupBaseDN": "dc=ldap,dc=domain,dc=tld",
        "GroupFilter": "(objectClass=account"
      }
    ],
    "Password": "readonly-password",
    "ReaderDN": "cn=readonly-account,dc=ldap,dc=domain,dc=tld",
    "SearchSettings": [
      {
        "BaseDN": "dc=ldap,dc=domain,dc=tld",
        "Filter": "(objectClass=account)",
        "UserNameAttribute": "uid"
      }
    ],
    "StartTLS": true,
    "TLSConfig": {
      "TLS": true,
      "TLSCACert": "/data/tls/ca.pem",
      "TLSCert": "/data/tls/cert.pem",
      "TLSKey": "/data/tls/key.pem",
      "TLSSkipVerify": false
    },
    "URL": "myldap.domain.tld:389"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="test-ldap-connectivity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ldap.checkPayload](#schemaldap.checkpayload)|true|details|
|» LDAPSettings|body|[portainer.LDAPSettings](#schemaportainer.ldapsettings)|false|none|

<h3 id="test-ldap-connectivity-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth, jwt
</aside>

|» » OrganisationName|body|string|false|none|
|» » UseOrganisation|body|boolean|false|none|
|» TLS|body|boolean|false|Use TLS|
|» Type|body|integer|true|Registry Type. Valid values are:<br>	1 (Quay.io),<br>	2 (Azure container registry),<br>	3 (custom registry),<br>	4 (Gitlab registry),<br>	5 (ProGet registry),<br>	6 (DockerHub)<br>	7 (ECR)|

|» Username|body|string|false|Username used to authenticate against this registry. Required when Authentication is true|

```bash
    ],
    "Type": 1,
    "Users": [

    ]
  }'
```

`POST /resource_controls`

Create a new resource control to restrict access to a Docker resource.
**Access policy**: administrator

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "AdministratorsOnly": true,
  "Public": true,
  "ResourceID": "617c5f22bb9b023d6daab7cba43a57576f83492867bc767d1c59416b065e5f08",
  "SubResourceIDs": [
    "617c5f22bb9b023d6daab7cba43a57576f83492867bc767d1c59416b065e5f08"
  ],
  "Teams": [
    56,
    7
  ],
  "Type": 1,
  "Users": [
    1,
    4
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-resource-control-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[resourcecontrols.resourceControlCreatePayload](#schemaresourcecontrols.resourcecontrolcreatepayload)|true|Resource control details|
|» AdministratorsOnly|body|boolean|false|Permit access to resource only to admins|
|» Public|body|boolean|false|Permit access to the associated resource to any user|
|» ResourceID|body|string|true|none|
|» SubResourceIDs|body|[string]|false|List of Docker resources that will inherit this access control|
|» Teams|body|[integer]|false|List of team identifiers with access to the associated resource|
|» Type|body|integer|true|Type of Resource. Valid values are: 1 - container, 2 - service<br>3 - volume, 4 - network, 5 - secret, 6 - stack, 7 - config, 8 - custom template, 9 - azure-container-group|
|» Users|body|[integer]|false|List of user identifiers with access to the associated resource|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» Type|1|
|» Type|2|
|» Type|3|
|» Type|4|
|» Type|5|
|» Type|6|
|» Type|7|
|» Type|8|
|» Type|9|

```json
      "UserId": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

## List stacks

<a id="opIdStackList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/stacks \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /stacks`

List all stacks based on the current user authorizations.
Will return all stacks if using an administrator account otherwise it
will only return the list of stacks the user have access to.
Limited stacks will not be returned by this endpoint.
**Access policy**: authenticated

<h3 id="list-stacks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filters|query|string|false|Filters to process on the stack list. Encoded as JSON (a map[string]string). For example, {'SwarmID': 'jpofkc0i9uo9wtx1zesuk649w'} will only return stacks that are part of the specified Swarm cluster. Available filters: EndpointID, SwarmID.|

<h3 id="list-stacks-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|Inline|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error|None|

<h3 id="list-stacks-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[portainer.Stack](#schemaportainer.stack)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth, jwt
</aside>

## Update a stack

<a id="opIdStackUpdate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://localhost:9443/api/stacks/0?endpointId=0' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "Env": [
      {
        "name": "name",
        "value": "value"
      }
    ],
    "Prune": true,
    "PullImage": false,
    "RepullImageAndRedeploy": true,
    "StackFileContent": "version: 3\n services:\n web:\n image:nginx"
  }'
```

`PUT /stacks/{id}`

Update a stack, only for file based stacks.
**Access policy**: authenticated

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "Env": [
    {
      "name": "name",
      "value": "value"
    }
  ],
  "Prune": true,
  "PullImage": false,
  "RepullImageAndRedeploy": true,
  "StackFileContent": "version: 3\n services:\n web:\n image:nginx"
}
```

|» RepullImageAndRedeploy|body|boolean|false|RepullImageAndRedeploy indicates whether to force repulling images and redeploying the stack|
|» StackFileContent|body|string|false|New content of the Stack file|

<a id="opIdStackUpdateGit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/stacks/0/git \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "AdditionalFiles": [
      "string"
    ],
    "AutoUpdate": {
      "ForcePullImage": false,
      "ForceUpdate": false,
      "Interval": "1m30s",
      "JobID": "15",
      "Webhook": "05de31a2-79fa-4644-9c12-faa67e5c49f0"
    },
    "ConfigFilePath": "string",
    "Env": [
      {
        "name": "name",
        "value": "value"
      }
    ],
    "Prune": true,
    "RepositoryAuthentication": true,
    "RepositoryPassword": "string",
    "RepositoryReferenceName": "string",
    "RepositoryURL": "string",
    "RepositoryUsername": "string",
    "SourceID": 0,
    "TLSSkipVerify": true
  }'
```

`POST /stacks/{id}/git`

Update the Git settings in a stack, e.g., RepositoryReferenceName and AutoUpdate. When SourceID is set, URL/auth/TLS are taken from the referenced Source.
**Access policy**: authenticated

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "AdditionalFiles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "AutoUpdate": {
    "ForcePullImage": false,
    "ForceUpdate": false,
    "Interval": "1m30s",
    "JobID": "15",
    "Webhook": "05de31a2-79fa-4644-9c12-faa67e5c49f0"
  },
  "ConfigFilePath": "string",
  "Env": [
    {
      "name": "name",
      "value": "value"
    }
  ],
  "Prune": true,
  "RepositoryAuthentication": true,
  "RepositoryPassword": "string",
  "RepositoryReferenceName": "string",
  "RepositoryURL": "string",
  "RepositoryUsername": "string",
  "SourceID": 0,
  "TLSSkipVerify": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-stacks-git-configs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Stack identifier|
|endpointId|query|integer|false|Stacks created before version 1.18.0 might not have an associated environment(endpoint) identifier. Use this optional parameter to set the environment(endpoint) identifier used by the stack.|
|body|body|[stacks.stackGitUpdatePayload](#schemastacks.stackgitupdatepayload)|true|Git configs for pull and redeploy a stack|
|» AdditionalFiles|body|[string]|false|none|
|» AutoUpdate|body|[portainer.AutoUpdateSettings](#schemaportainer.autoupdatesettings)|false|none|
|» ConfigFilePath|body|string|false|none|
|» Env|body|[[portainer.Pair](#schemaportainer.pair)]|false|none|

## Migrate a stack to another environment(endpoint)

<a id="opIdStackMigrate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://localhost:9443/api/stacks/0/migrate \

  }'
```

`POST /stacks/{id}/migrate`

Migrate a stack from an environment(endpoint) to another environment(endpoint). It will re-create the stack inside the target environment(endpoint) before removing the original stack.
**Access policy**: authenticated

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "EndpointID": 2,
  "Name": "new-stack",
  "SwarmID": "jpofkc0i9uo9wtx1zesuk649w"
}
```

<h3 id="migrate-a-stack-to-another-environmentendpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|Stack identifier|
|endpointId|query|integer|false|Stacks created before version 1.18.0 might not have an associated environment(endpoint) identifier. Use this optional parameter to set the environment(endpoint) identifier used by the stack.|
|body|body|[stacks.stackMigratePayload](#schemastacks.stackmigratepayload)|true|Stack migration details|
|» EndpointID|body|integer|true|Environment(Endpoint) identifier of the target environment(endpoint) where the stack will be relocated|
|» Name|body|string|false|If provided will rename the migrated stack|
|» SwarmID|body|string|false|Swarm cluster identifier, must match the identifier of the cluster where the stack will be relocated|

|» AdditionalFiles|body|[string]|false|Applicable when deploying with multiple stack files|

|» » JobID|body|string|false|Autoupdate job id|
|» » Webhook|body|string|false|A UUID generated from client|
|» ComposeFile|body|string|false|Path to the Stack file inside the Git repository|
|» Env|body|[[portainer.Pair](#schemaportainer.pair)]|false|A list of environment variables used during stack deployment|
|» FromAppTemplate|body|boolean|false|Whether the stack is from a app template|
|» Name|body|string|true|Name of the stack|
|» RepositoryAuthentication|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Use basic authentication to clone the Git repository.|
|» RepositoryPassword|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Password used in basic authentication.|
|» RepositoryReferenceName|body|string|false|Reference name of a Git repository hosting the Stack file|
|» RepositoryURL|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. URL of a Git repository hosting the Stack file.|
|» RepositoryUsername|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Username used in basic authentication.|
|» SourceID|body|integer|false|SourceID references an existing Source for git credentials/URL.<br>When set, the inline URL and authentication fields are ignored.|
|» TLSSkipVerify|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. TLSSkipVerify skips SSL verification when cloning the Git repository.|

|» AdditionalFiles|body|[string]|false|Applicable when deploying with multiple stack files|
|» AutoUpdate|body|object|false|Optional GitOps update configuration|
|» » ForcePullImage|body|boolean|false|Pull latest image|
|» » ForceUpdate|body|boolean|false|Force update ignores repo changes|
|» » Interval|body|string|false|Auto update interval<br>Deprecated: polling interval now lives on the associated Source (Source.Interval).<br>Kept for DB backwards-compatibility only; new code must not read or write this field.|
|» » JobID|body|string|false|Autoupdate job id|
|» » Webhook|body|string|false|A UUID generated from client|
|» ComposeFile|body|string|false|Path to the Stack file inside the Git repository|
|» Env|body|[[portainer.Pair](#schemaportainer.pair)]|false|A list of environment variables used during stack deployment|
|» FromAppTemplate|body|boolean|false|Whether the stack is from a app template|
|» Name|body|string|true|Name of the stack|
|» RepositoryAuthentication|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Use basic authentication to clone the Git repository.|
|» RepositoryPassword|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Password used in basic authentication.|
|» RepositoryReferenceName|body|string|false|Reference name of a Git repository hosting the Stack file|
|» RepositoryURL|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. URL of a Git repository hosting the Stack file.|
|» RepositoryUsername|body|string|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. Username used in basic authentication.|
|» SourceID|body|integer|false|SourceID references an existing Source for git credentials/URL.<br>When set, the inline URL and authentication fields are ignored.|
|» SwarmID|body|string|true|Swarm cluster identifier|
|» TLSSkipVerify|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: use SourceID instead. TLSSkipVerify skips SSL verification when cloning the Git repository.|

(user-endpoint, user-group, team-endpoint, team-group).
Environments where the user has no role are omitted.
**Access policy**: restricted

<h3 id="inspect-a-users-effective-access-on-every-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|User identifier|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "accessLocation": "environment",
    "endpointId": 0,
    "endpointName": "string",
    "groupId": 0,
    "groupName": "string",
    "roleId": 0,
    "roleName": "string",
    "rolePriority": 0,
    "teamId": 0,
    "teamName": "string"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="inspect-a-users-effective-access-on-every-environment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|Inline|

|500|Internal Server Error|Server error|None|

<h1 id="portainerce-api-websocket">websocket</h1>

## Attach a websocket

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://localhost:9443/api/websocket/attach?endpointId=0' \
  -H "X-API-KEY: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /websocket/attach`

If the nodeName query parameter is present, the request will be proxied to the underlying agent environment(endpoint).
If the nodeName query parameter is not specified, the request will be upgraded to the websocket protocol and
an AttachStart operation HTTP request will be created and hijacked.
**Access policy**: authenticated

<h3 id="attach-a-websocket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|endpointId|query|integer|true|environment(endpoint) ID of the environment(endpoint) where the resource is located|
|nodeName|query|string|false|node name|

<h3 id="attach-a-websocket-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth, jwt
</aside>

```json
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ForceRecreate|boolean|false|none|ForceRecreate is a flag indicating if the agent must force the redeployment of the stack.<br>This field is only used when the Force Redeployment is triggered.<br>Once the stack is redeployed, this field will be reset to false.<br>For standard edge agent, this field is used in agent side<br>For async edge agent, this field is used in both agent side and server side.<br>This flag drives `docker compose up --force-recreate` option|
|Prune|boolean|false|none|Prune is a flag indicating if the agent must prune the containers or not when creating/updating an edge stack<br>This flag drives `docker compose up --remove-orphans` and `docker stack up --prune` options<br>Used only for EE|
|RemoveVolumes|boolean|false|none|RemoveVolumes is a flag indicating if the agent must remove the named volumes declared<br>in the compose file and anonymouse volumes attached to containers<br>This flag drives `docker compose down --volumes` option<br>Used only for EE|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|AlwaysCloneGitRepoForRelativePath|boolean|false|none|AlwaysCloneGitRepoForRelativePath is a flag indicating if the agent must always clone the git repository for relative path.<br>This field is only valid when SupportRelativePath is true.<br>Used only for EE|
|CreatedBy|string|false|none|CreatedBy is the username that created this stack<br>Used for adding labels to Kubernetes manifests|
|CreatedByUserId|string|false|none|CreatedByUserId is the user ID that created this stack<br>Used for adding labels to Kubernetes manifests|
|DeployerOptionsPayload|[edge.DeployerOptionsPayload](#schemaedge.deployeroptionspayload)|false|none|none|
|DirEntries|[[filesystem.DirEntry](#schemafilesystem.direntry)]|false|none|Content of stack folder|
|EdgeUpdateID|integer|false|none|EdgeUpdateID is the ID of the edge update related to this stack.<br>Used only for EE|
|EntryFileName|string|false|none|Name of the stack entry file|
|EnvVars|[[portainer.Pair](#schemaportainer.pair)]|false|none|Used only for EE<br>EnvVars is a list of environment variables to inject into the stack|
|FilesystemPath|string|false|none|Mount point for relative path|
|ForceUpdate|boolean|false|none|ForceUpdate is a flag indicating if the agent must force the update of the stack.<br>Used only for EE|
|HelmConfig|object|false|none|HelmConfig represents the Helm configuration for an edge stack|
|ID|integer|false|none|ID of the stack|
|Name|string|false|none|Name of the stack|
|Namespace|string|false|none|Namespace to use for kubernetes stack. Keep empty to use the manifest namespace.|
|PrePullImage|boolean|false|none|PrePullImage is a flag indicating if the agent must pull the image before deploying the stack.<br>Used only for EE|
|RePullImage|boolean|false|none|RePullImage is a flag indicating if the agent must pull the image if it is already present on the node.<br>Used only for EE|
|ReadyRePullImage|boolean|false|none|Used only for EE async edge agent<br>ReadyRePullImage is a flag to indicate whether the auto update is trigger to re-pull image<br>Deprecated(2.36): use DeployerOptionsPayload.ForceRecreate instead|
|RegistryCredentials|[[edge.RegistryCredentials](#schemaedge.registrycredentials)]|false|none|RegistryCredentials holds the credentials for a Docker registry.<br>Used only for EE|
|RetryDeploy|boolean|false|none|RetryDeploy is a flag indicating if the agent must retry to deploy the stack if it fails.<br>Used only for EE|
|RetryPeriod|integer|false|none|RetryPeriod specifies the duration, in seconds, for which the agent should continue attempting to deploy the stack after a failure<br>Used only for EE|
|RollbackTo|integer|false|none|RollbackTo specifies the stack file version to rollback to (only support to rollback to the last version currently)|
|StackFileContent|string|false|none|Content of the stack file (for compatibility to agent version less than 2.19.0)|
|SupportPerDeviceConfigs|boolean|false|none|Whether the edge stack supports per device configs|
|SupportRelativePath|boolean|false|none|Is relative path supported|
|Version|integer|false|none|Version of the stack file|

```json
{
  "DeploymentType": 0,
  "EdgeGroups": [
    1
  ],
  "FilePathInRepository": "docker-compose.yml",
  "Name": "stack-name",
  "Registries": [
    0
  ],
  "RepositoryAuthentication": true,
  "RepositoryPassword": "myGitPassword",
  "RepositoryReferenceName": "refs/heads/master",
  "RepositoryURL": "https://github.com/openfaas/faas",
  "RepositoryUsername": "myGitUsername",
  "SourceID": 1,
  "TLSSkipVerify": false,
  "UseManifestNamespaces": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|DeploymentType|integer|false|none|Deployment type to deploy this stack<br>Valid values are: 0 - 'compose', 1 - 'kubernetes'<br>compose is enabled only for docker environments<br>kubernetes is enabled only for kubernetes environments|
|EdgeGroups|[integer]|true|none|List of identifiers of EdgeGroups|
|FilePathInRepository|string|false|none|Path to the Stack file inside the Git repository|
|Name|string|true|none|Name of the stack<br>Max length: 255<br>Name must only contains lowercase characters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores<br>Name must start with a lowercase character or number<br>Example: stack-name or stack_123 or stackName|
|Registries|[integer]|false|none|List of Registries to use for this stack|
|RepositoryAuthentication|boolean|false|none|Deprecated: Use SourceID instead. Use basic authentication to clone the Git repository.|
|RepositoryPassword|string|false|none|Deprecated: Use SourceID instead. Password used in basic authentication.|
|RepositoryReferenceName|string|false|none|Reference name of a Git repository hosting the Stack file|
|RepositoryURL|string|false|none|Deprecated: Use SourceID instead. URL of a Git repository hosting the Stack file.|
|RepositoryUsername|string|false|none|Deprecated: Use SourceID instead. Username used in basic authentication.|
|SourceID|integer|false|none|SourceID references an existing Source for git credentials/URL.<br>When set, the inline URL and authentication fields are ignored.|
|TLSSkipVerify|boolean|false|none|Deprecated: Use SourceID instead. TLSSkipVerify skips SSL verification when cloning the Git repository.|
|UseManifestNamespaces|boolean|false|none|Uses the manifest's namespaces instead of the default one|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|DeploymentType|0|
|DeploymentType|1|
|DeploymentType|2|

```json
{
  "DeleteEmptyDirData": true,
  "DisableEviction": false,
  "Force": false,
  "GracePeriodSeconds": -1,
  "IgnoreDaemonSets": true,
  "TimeoutSeconds": 60
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|DeleteEmptyDirData|boolean|false|none|DeleteEmptyDirData allows eviction of pods using emptyDir volumes, whose data is lost once the pod is deleted.|
|DisableEviction|boolean|false|none|DisableEviction forces the use of direct pod deletion instead of the eviction API, ignoring any configured PodDisruptionBudgets.|
|Force|boolean|false|none|Force allows deletion of standalone pods not managed by a controller.|
|GracePeriodSeconds|integer|false|none|GracePeriodSeconds overrides each pod's termination grace period. -1 uses the pod's own grace period.|
|IgnoreDaemonSets|boolean|false|none|IgnoreDaemonSets skips DaemonSet-managed pods, which would otherwise block the drain.|
|TimeoutSeconds|integer|false|none|TimeoutSeconds is the overall time to wait for the drain to complete. Defaults to 60 when omitted.|

<h2 id="tocS_portainer.HelmConfig">portainer.HelmConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaportainer.helmconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_portainer.HelmConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSportainer.helmconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsportainer.helmconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "Atomic": true,
  "ChartName": "nginx",
  "ChartPath": "charts/my-app",
  "ChartURL": "https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami",
  "ChartVersion": "15.0.0",
  "Namespace": "default",
  "Timeout": "5m0s",
  "ValuesFiles": [
    "['values/prod.yaml'",
    " 'values/secrets.yaml']"
  ],
  "ValuesInline": "replicaCount: 2"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Atomic|boolean|false|none|Atomic enables automatic rollback on deployment failure (equivalent to helm --atomic).<br>Used by both git repo and Helm repository deployments.|
|ChartName|string|false|none|ChartName is the name of the Helm chart within the repository.<br>Required for Helm repository deployments.|
|ChartPath|string|false|none|ChartPath is the path to a Helm chart folder within the cloned git repository.<br>Used exclusively for git repo helm deployments. Mutually exclusive with ChartURL.|
|ChartURL|string|false|none|ChartURL is the URL of a Helm chart repository.<br>Used exclusively for Helm repository deployments. Mutually exclusive with ChartPath.|
|ChartVersion|string|false|none|ChartVersion is the version of the Helm chart to deploy. Empty means latest.<br>Used exclusively for Helm repository deployments.|
|Namespace|string|false|none|Namespace is the Kubernetes namespace to deploy the Helm chart into.<br>Used by both git repo and Helm repository deployments.|
|Timeout|string|false|none|Timeout sets the deadline for Helm operations (equivalent to helm --timeout, e.g. "5m0s").<br>Used by both git repo and Helm repository deployments.|
|ValuesFiles|[string]|false|none|ValuesFiles is a list of relative paths to Helm values YAML files within the cloned git repository.<br>Used exclusively for git repo helm deployments.|
|ValuesInline|string|false|none|ValuesInline is the inline YAML string of Helm values.<br>Used exclusively for Helm repository deployments.|

```json
}
```

|TLSConfig|[portainer.TLSConfiguration](#schemaportainer.tlsconfiguration)|false|none|none|
|URL|string|false|none|URL or IP address of the LDAP server|

|UpdatedBy|string|false|none|The username which last updated this stack|

<h2 id="tocS_portainer.Template">portainer.Template</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaportainer.template"></a>
<a id="schema_portainer.Template"></a>
<a id="tocSportainer.template"></a>
<a id="tocsportainer.template"></a>

```json
{
  "administrator_only": true,
  "categories": [
    "database"
  ],
  "command": "ls -lah",
  "description": "High performance web server",
  "env": [
    {
      "default": "default_value",
      "description": "MySQL root account password",
      "label": "Root password",
      "name": "MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD",
      "preset": false,
      "select": [
        {
          "default": false,
          "text": "text value",
          "value": "value"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "hostname": "mycontainer",
  "id": 1,
  "image": "nginx:latest",
  "interactive": true,
  "labels": [
    {
      "name": "name",
      "value": "value"
    }
  ],
  "logo": "https://portainer.io/img/logo.svg",
  "name": "mystackname",
  "network": "mynet",
  "note": "This is my <b>custom</b> template",
  "platform": "linux",
  "ports": [
    "8080:80/tcp"
  ],
  "privileged": true,
  "registry": "quay.io",
  "repository": {
    "stackfile": "./subfolder/docker-compose.yml",
    "url": "https://github.com/portainer/portainer-compose"
  },
  "restart_policy": "on-failure",
  "stackFile": "string",
  "title": "Nginx",
  "type": 1,
  "volumes": [
    {
      "bind": "/tmp",
      "container": "/data",
      "readonly": true
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|administrator_only|boolean|false|none|Whether the template should be available to administrators only|
|categories|[string]|false|none|A list of categories associated to the template|
|command|string|false|none|The command that will be executed in a container template|
|description|string|false|none|Description of the template|
|env|[[portainer.TemplateEnv](#schemaportainer.templateenv)]|false|none|A list of environment(endpoint) variables used during the template deployment|
|hostname|string|false|none|Container hostname|
|id|integer|false|none|Mandatory container/stack fields<br>Template Identifier|
|image|string|false|none|Mandatory container fields<br>Image associated to a container template. Mandatory for a container template|
|interactive|boolean|false|none|Whether the container should be started in<br>interactive mode (-i -t equivalent on the CLI)|
|labels|[[portainer.Pair](#schemaportainer.pair)]|false|none|Container labels|
|logo|string|false|none|URL of the template's logo|
|name|string|false|none|Optional stack/container fields<br>Default name for the stack/container to be used on deployment|
|network|string|false|none|Name of a network that will be used on container deployment if it exists inside the environment(endpoint)|
|note|string|false|none|A note that will be displayed in the UI. Supports HTML content|
|platform|string|false|none|Platform associated to the template.<br>Valid values are: 'linux', 'windows' or leave empty for multi-platform|
|ports|[string]|false|none|A list of ports exposed by the container|
|privileged|boolean|false|none|Whether the container should be started in privileged mode|
|registry|string|false|none|Optional container fields<br>The URL of a registry associated to the image for a container template|
|repository|object|false|none|Mandatory stack fields|
|restart_policy|string|false|none|Container restart policy|
|stackFile|string|false|none|Mandatory Edge stack fields<br>Stack file used for this template|
|title|string|false|none|Title of the template|
|type|object|false|none|Template type. Valid values are: 1 (container), 2 (Swarm stack), 3 (Compose stack), 4 (Compose edge stack)|
|volumes|[[portainer.TemplateVolume](#schemaportainer.templatevolume)]|false|none|A list of volumes used during the container template deployment|

|Env|[[portainer.Pair](#schemaportainer.pair)]|false|none|A list of environment(endpoint) variables used during stack deployment|

|ResourceControl|[portainer.ResourceControl](#schemaportainer.resourcecontrol)|false|none|none|
|Status|object|false|none|Stack status (1 - active, 2 - inactive, 3 - deploying, 4 - error)|
|SwarmId|string|false|none|Cluster identifier of the Swarm cluster where the stack is deployed|
|Type|object|false|none|Stack type. 1 for a Swarm stack, 2 for a Compose stack|
|UpdateDate|integer|false|none|The date in unix time when stack was last updated|
|UpdatedBy|string|false|none|The username which last updated this stack|

<h2 id="tocS_v1.AWSElasticBlockStoreVolumeSource">v1.AWSElasticBlockStoreVolumeSource</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemav1.awselasticblockstorevolumesource"></a>
<a id="schema_v1.AWSElasticBlockStoreVolumeSource"></a>
<a id="tocSv1.awselasticblockstorevolumesource"></a>
<a id="tocsv1.awselasticblockstorevolumesource"></a>

```json
{
  "fsType": "string",
  "partition": 0,
  "readOnly": true,
  "volumeID": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fsType|string|false|none|fsType is the filesystem type of the volume that you want to mount.<br>Tip: Ensure that the filesystem type is supported by the host operating system.<br>Examples: "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs". Implicitly inferred to be "ext4" if unspecified.<br>More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes#awselasticblockstore<br>TODO: how do we prevent errors in the filesystem from compromising the machine<br>+optional|
|partition|integer|false|none|partition is the partition in the volume that you want to mount.<br>If omitted, the default is to mount by volume name.<br>Examples: For volume /dev/sda1, you specify the partition as "1".<br>Similarly, the volume partition for /dev/sda is "0" (or you can leave the property empty).<br>+optional|
|readOnly|boolean|false|none|readOnly value true will force the readOnly setting in VolumeMounts.<br>More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes#awselasticblockstore<br>+optional|
|volumeID|string|false|none|volumeID is unique ID of the persistent disk resource in AWS (Amazon EBS volume).<br>More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes#awselasticblockstore|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cachingMode|object|false|none|cachingMode is the Host Caching mode: None, Read Only, Read Write.<br>+optional<br>+default=ref(AzureDataDiskCachingReadWrite)|
|diskName|string|false|none|diskName is the Name of the data disk in the blob storage|
|diskURI|string|false|none|diskURI is the URI of data disk in the blob storage|
|fsType|string|false|none|fsType is Filesystem type to mount.<br>Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system.<br>Ex. "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs". Implicitly inferred to be "ext4" if unspecified.<br>+optional<br>+default="ext4"|
|kind|object|false|none|kind expected values are Shared: multiple blob disks per storage account  Dedicated: single blob disk per storage account  Managed: azure managed data disk (only in managed availability set). defaults to shared<br>+default=ref(AzureSharedBlobDisk)|
|readOnly|boolean|false|none|readOnly Defaults to false (read/write). ReadOnly here will force<br>the ReadOnly setting in VolumeMounts.<br>+optional<br>+default=false|

|controllerPublishSecretRef|object|false|none|controllerPublishSecretRef is a reference to the secret object containing<br>sensitive information to pass to the CSI driver to complete the CSI<br>ControllerPublishVolume and ControllerUnpublishVolume calls.<br>This field is optional, and may be empty if no secret is required. If the<br>secret object contains more than one secret, all secrets are passed.<br>+optional|
|driver|string|false|none|driver is the name of the driver to use for this volume.<br>Required.|
|fsType|string|false|none|fsType to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system.<br>Ex. "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs".<br>+optional|
|nodeExpandSecretRef|object|false|none|nodeExpandSecretRef is a reference to the secret object containing<br>sensitive information to pass to the CSI driver to complete the CSI<br>NodeExpandVolume call.<br>This field is optional, may be omitted if no secret is required. If the<br>secret object contains more than one secret, all secrets are passed.<br>+optional|
|nodePublishSecretRef|object|false|none|nodePublishSecretRef is a reference to the secret object containing<br>sensitive information to pass to the CSI driver to complete the CSI<br>NodePublishVolume and NodeUnpublishVolume calls.<br>This field is optional, and may be empty if no secret is required. If the<br>secret object contains more than one secret, all secrets are passed.<br>+optional|
|nodeStageSecretRef|object|false|none|nodeStageSecretRef is a reference to the secret object containing sensitive<br>information to pass to the CSI driver to complete the CSI NodeStageVolume<br>and NodeStageVolume and NodeUnstageVolume calls.<br>This field is optional, and may be empty if no secret is required. If the<br>secret object contains more than one secret, all secrets are passed.<br>+optional|
|readOnly|boolean|false|none|readOnly value to pass to ControllerPublishVolumeRequest.<br>Defaults to false (read/write).<br>+optional|
|volumeAttributes|object|false|none|volumeAttributes of the volume to publish.<br>+optional|
|volumeHandle|string|false|none|volumeHandle is the unique volume name returned by the CSI volume<br>plugin’s CreateVolume to refer to the volume on all subsequent calls.<br>Required.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|driver|string|false|none|driver is the name of the CSI driver that handles this volume.<br>Consult with your admin for the correct name as registered in the cluster.|
|fsType|string|false|none|fsType to mount. Ex. "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs".<br>If not provided, the empty value is passed to the associated CSI driver<br>which will determine the default filesystem to apply.<br>+optional|
|nodePublishSecretRef|object|false|none|nodePublishSecretRef is a reference to the secret object containing<br>sensitive information to pass to the CSI driver to complete the CSI<br>NodePublishVolume and NodeUnpublishVolume calls.<br>This field is optional, and  may be empty if no secret is required. If the<br>secret object contains more than one secret, all secret references are passed.<br>+optional|
|readOnly|boolean|false|none|readOnly specifies a read-only configuration for the volume.<br>Defaults to false (read/write).<br>+optional|
|volumeAttributes|object|false|none|volumeAttributes stores driver-specific properties that are passed to the CSI<br>driver. Consult your driver's documentation for supported values.<br>+optional|

|monitors|[string]|false|none|monitors is Required: Monitors is a collection of Ceph monitors<br>More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/cephfs/README.md#how-to-use-it<br>+listType=atomic|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|labelSelector|object|false|none|Select all ClusterTrustBundles that match this label selector.  Only has<br>effect if signerName is set.  Mutually-exclusive with name.  If unset,<br>interpreted as "match nothing".  If set but empty, interpreted as "match<br>everything".<br>+optional|
|name|string|false|none|Select a single ClusterTrustBundle by object name.  Mutually-exclusive<br>with signerName and labelSelector.<br>+optional|
|optional|boolean|false|none|If true, don't block pod startup if the referenced ClusterTrustBundle(s)<br>aren't available.  If using name, then the named ClusterTrustBundle is<br>allowed not to exist.  If using signerName, then the combination of<br>signerName and labelSelector is allowed to match zero<br>ClusterTrustBundles.<br>+optional|
|path|string|false|none|Relative path from the volume root to write the bundle.|
|signerName|string|false|none|Select all ClusterTrustBundles that match this signer name.<br>Mutually-exclusive with name.  The contents of all selected<br>ClusterTrustBundles will be unified and deduplicated.<br>+optional|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|defaultMode|integer|false|none|defaultMode is optional: mode bits used to set permissions on created files by default.<br>Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or a decimal value between 0 and 511.<br>YAML accepts both octal and decimal values, JSON requires decimal values for mode bits.<br>Defaults to 0644.<br>Directories within the path are not affected by this setting.<br>This might be in conflict with other options that affect the file<br>mode, like fsGroup, and the result can be other mode bits set.<br>+optional|
|items|[[v1.KeyToPath](#schemav1.keytopath)]|false|none|items if unspecified, each key-value pair in the Data field of the referenced<br>ConfigMap will be projected into the volume as a file whose name is the<br>key and content is the value. If specified, the listed keys will be<br>projected into the specified paths, and unlisted keys will not be<br>present. If a key is specified which is not present in the ConfigMap,<br>the volume setup will error unless it is marked optional. Paths must be<br>relative and may not contain the '..' path or start with '..'.<br>+optional<br>+listType=atomic|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the referent.<br>This field is effectively required, but due to backwards compatibility is<br>allowed to be empty. Instances of this type with an empty value here are<br>almost certainly wrong.<br>More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names<br>+optional<br>+default=""<br>+kubebuilder:default=""<br>TODO: Drop `kubebuilder:default` when controller-gen doesn't need it https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubebuilder/issues/3896.|
|optional|boolean|false|none|optional specify whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined<br>+optional|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lastTransitionTime|string|false|none|Last time the condition transitioned from one status to another.|
|lastUpdateTime|string|false|none|The last time this condition was updated.|
|message|string|false|none|A human readable message indicating details about the transition.|
|reason|string|false|none|The reason for the condition's last transition.|
|status|object|false|none|Status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.|
|type|object|false|none|Type of deployment condition.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|minReadySeconds|integer|false|none|Minimum number of seconds for which a newly created pod should be ready<br>without any of its container crashing, for it to be considered available.<br>Defaults to 0 (pod will be considered available as soon as it is ready)<br>+optional|
|paused|boolean|false|none|Indicates that the deployment is paused.<br>+optional|
|progressDeadlineSeconds|integer|false|none|The maximum time in seconds for a deployment to make progress before it<br>is considered to be failed. The deployment controller will continue to<br>process failed deployments and a condition with a ProgressDeadlineExceeded<br>reason will be surfaced in the deployment status. Note that progress will<br>not be estimated during the time a deployment is paused. Defaults to 600s.|
|replicas|integer|false|none|Number of desired pods. This is a pointer to distinguish between explicit<br>zero and not specified. Defaults to 1.<br>+optional|
|revisionHistoryLimit|integer|false|none|The number of old ReplicaSets to retain to allow rollback.<br>This is a pointer to distinguish between explicit zero and not specified.<br>Defaults to 10.<br>+optional|
|selector|object|false|none|Label selector for pods. Existing ReplicaSets whose pods are<br>selected by this will be the ones affected by this deployment.<br>It must match the pod template's labels.|
|strategy|object|false|none|The deployment strategy to use to replace existing pods with new ones.<br>+optional<br>+patchStrategy=retainKeys|
|template|object|false|none|Template describes the pods that will be created.<br>The only allowed template.spec.restartPolicy value is "Always".|

<h2 id="tocS_v1.DeploymentStatus">v1.DeploymentStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemav1.deploymentstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_v1.DeploymentStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSv1.deploymentstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsv1.deploymentstatus"></a>

```json
{
  "availableReplicas": 0,
  "collisionCount": 0,
  "conditions": [
    {
      "lastTransitionTime": "string",
      "lastUpdateTime": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "reason": "string",
      "status": {},
      "type": {}
    }
  ],
  "observedGeneration": 0,
  "readyReplicas": 0,
  "replicas": 0,
  "terminatingReplicas": 0,
  "unavailableReplicas": 0,
  "updatedReplicas": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|availableReplicas|integer|false|none|Total number of available non-terminating pods (ready for at least minReadySeconds) targeted by this deployment.<br>+optional|
|collisionCount|integer|false|none|Count of hash collisions for the Deployment. The Deployment controller uses this<br>field as a collision avoidance mechanism when it needs to create the name for the<br>newest ReplicaSet.<br>+optional|
|conditions|[[v1.DeploymentCondition](#schemav1.deploymentcondition)]|false|none|Represents the latest available observations of a deployment's current state.<br>+patchMergeKey=type<br>+patchStrategy=merge<br>+listType=map<br>+listMapKey=type|
|observedGeneration|integer|false|none|The generation observed by the deployment controller.<br>+optional|
|readyReplicas|integer|false|none|Total number of non-terminating pods targeted by this Deployment with a Ready Condition.<br>+optional|
|replicas|integer|false|none|Total number of non-terminating pods targeted by this deployment (their labels match the selector).<br>+optional|
|terminatingReplicas|integer|false|none|Total number of terminating pods targeted by this deployment. Terminating pods have a non-null<br>.metadata.deletionTimestamp and have not yet reached the Failed or Succeeded .status.phase.<br><br>This is a beta field and requires enabling DeploymentReplicaSetTerminatingReplicas feature (enabled by default).<br>+optional|
|unavailableReplicas|integer|false|none|Total number of unavailable pods targeted by this deployment. This is the total number of<br>pods that are still required for the deployment to have 100% available capacity. They may<br>either be pods that are running but not yet available or pods that still have not been created.<br>+optional|

Not executed within a shell.<br>The image's ENTRYPOINT is used if this is not provided.<br>Variable references $(VAR_NAME) are expanded using the container's environment. If a variable<br>cannot be resolved, the reference in the input string will be unchanged. Double $$ are reduced<br>to a single $, which allows for escaping the $(VAR_NAME) syntax: i.e. "$$(VAR_NAME)" will<br>produce the string literal "$(VAR_NAME)". Escaped references will never be expanded, regardless<br>of whether the variable exists or not. Cannot be updated.<br>More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/inject-data-application/define-command-argument-container/#running-a-command-in-a-shell<br>+optional<br>+listType=atomic|
|env|[[v1.EnvVar](#schemav1.envvar)]|false|none|List of environment variables to set in the container.<br>Cannot be updated.<br>+optional<br>+patchMergeKey=name<br>+patchStrategy=merge<br>+listType=map<br>+listMapKey=name|
|envFrom|[[v1.EnvFromSource](#schemav1.envfromsource)]|false|none|List of sources to populate environment variables in the container.<br>The keys defined within a source may consist of any printable ASCII characters except '='.<br>When a key exists in multiple<br>sources, the value associated with the last source will take precedence.<br>Values defined by an Env with a duplicate key will take precedence.<br>Cannot be updated.<br>+optional<br>+listType=atomic|

|imagePullPolicy|object|false|none|Image pull policy.<br>One of Always, Never, IfNotPresent.<br>Defaults to Always if :latest tag is specified, or IfNotPresent otherwise.<br>Cannot be updated.<br>More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images#updating-images<br>+optional|
|lifecycle|object|false|none|Lifecycle is not allowed for ephemeral containers.<br>+optional|
|livenessProbe|object|false|none|Probes are not allowed for ephemeral containers.<br>+optional|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the ephemeral container specified as a DNS_LABEL.<br>This name must be unique among all containers, init containers and ephemeral containers.|

|restartPolicy|object|false|none|Restart policy for the container to manage the restart behavior of each<br>container within a pod.<br>You cannot set this field on ephemeral containers.<br>+optional|

If stdinOnce is set to true, stdin is opened on container start, is empty until the<br>first client attaches to stdin, and then remains open and accepts data until the client disconnects,<br>at which time stdin is closed and remains closed until the container is restarted. If this<br>flag is false, a container processes that reads from stdin will never receive an EOF.<br>Default is false<br>+optional|
|targetContainerName|string|false|none|If set, the name of the container from PodSpec that this ephemeral container targets.<br>The ephemeral container will be run in the namespaces (IPC, PID, etc) of this container.<br>If not set then the ephemeral container uses the namespaces configured in the Pod spec.<br><br>The container runtime must implement support for this feature. If the runtime does not<br>support namespace targeting then the result of setting this field is undefined.<br>+optional|
|terminationMessagePath|string|false|none|Optional: Path at which the file to which the container's termination message<br>will be written is mounted into the container's filesystem.<br>Message written is intended to be brief final status, such as an assertion failure message.<br>Will be truncated by the node if greater than 4096 bytes. The total message length across<br>all containers will be limited to 12kb.<br>Defaults to /dev/termination-log.<br>Cannot be updated.<br>+optional|
|terminationMessagePolicy|object|false|none|Indicate how the termination message should be populated. File will use the contents of<br>terminationMessagePath to populate the container status message on both success and failure.<br>FallbackToLogsOnError will use the last chunk of container log output if the termination<br>message file is empty and the container exited with an error.<br>The log output is limited to 2048 bytes or 80 lines, whichever is smaller.<br>Defaults to File.<br>Cannot be updated.<br>+optional|
|tty|boolean|false|none|Whether this container should allocate a TTY for itself, also requires 'stdin' to be true.<br>Default is false.<br>+optional|
|volumeDevices|[[v1.VolumeDevice](#schemav1.volumedevice)]|false|none|volumeDevices is the list of block devices to be used by the container.<br>+patchMergeKey=devicePath<br>+patchStrategy=merge<br>+listType=map<br>+listMapKey=devicePath<br>+optional|
|volumeMounts|[[v1.VolumeMount](#schemav1.volumemount)]|false|none|Pod volumes to mount into the container's filesystem. Subpath mounts are not allowed for ephemeral containers.<br>Cannot be updated.<br>+optional<br>+patchMergeKey=mountPath<br>+patchStrategy=merge<br>+listType=map<br>+listMapKey=mountPath|
|workingDir|string|false|none|Container's working directory.<br>If not specified, the container runtime's default will be used, which<br>might be configured in the container image.<br>Cannot be updated.<br>+optional|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|volumeClaimTemplate|object|false|none|Will be used to create a stand-alone PVC to provision the volume.<br>The pod in which this EphemeralVolumeSource is embedded will be the<br>owner of the PVC, i.e. the PVC will be deleted together with the<br>pod.  The name of the PVC will be `<pod name>-<volume name>` where<br>`<volume name>` is the name from the `PodSpec.Volumes` array<br>entry. Pod validation will reject the pod if the concatenated name<br>is not valid for a PVC (for example, too long).<br><br>An existing PVC with that name that is not owned by the pod<br>will *not* be used for the pod to avoid using an unrelated<br>volume by mistake. Starting the pod is then blocked until<br>the unrelated PVC is removed. If such a pre-created PVC is<br>meant to be used by the pod, the PVC has to updated with an<br>owner reference to the pod once the pod exists. Normally<br>this should not be necessary, but it may be useful when<br>manually reconstructing a broken cluster.<br><br>This field is read-only and no changes will be made by Kubernetes<br>to the PVC after it has been created.<br><br>Required, must not be nil.|

|active|object|false|none|Active reports the checkpointed config the node is actively using.<br>Active will represent either the current version of the Assigned config,<br>or the current LastKnownGood config, depending on whether attempting to use the<br>Assigned config results in an error.<br>+optional|
|assigned|object|false|none|Assigned reports the checkpointed config the node will try to use.<br>When Node.Spec.ConfigSource is updated, the node checkpoints the associated<br>config payload to local disk, along with a record indicating intended<br>config. The node refers to this record to choose its config checkpoint, and<br>reports this record in Assigned. Assigned only updates in the status after<br>the record has been checkpointed to disk. When the Kubelet is restarted,<br>it tries to make the Assigned config the Active config by loading and<br>validating the checkpointed payload identified by Assigned.<br>+optional|
|error|string|false|none|Error describes any problems reconciling the Spec.ConfigSource to the Active config.<br>Errors may occur, for example, attempting to checkpoint Spec.ConfigSource to the local Assigned<br>record, attempting to checkpoint the payload associated with Spec.ConfigSource, attempting<br>to load or validate the Assigned config, etc.<br>Errors may occur at different points while syncing config. Earlier errors (e.g. download or<br>checkpointing errors) will not result in a rollback to LastKnownGood, and may resolve across<br>Kubelet retries. Later errors (e.g. loading or validating a checkpointed config) will result in<br>a rollback to LastKnownGood. In the latter case, it is usually possible to resolve the error<br>by fixing the config assigned in Spec.ConfigSource.<br>You can find additional information for debugging by searching the error message in the Kubelet log.<br>Error is a human-readable description of the error state; machines can check whether or not Error<br>is empty, but should not rely on the stability of the Error text across Kubelet versions.<br>+optional|
|lastKnownGood|object|false|none|LastKnownGood reports the checkpointed config the node will fall back to<br>when it encounters an error attempting to use the Assigned config.<br>The Assigned config becomes the LastKnownGood config when the node determines<br>that the Assigned config is stable and correct.<br>This is currently implemented as a 10-minute soak period starting when the local<br>record of Assigned config is updated. If the Assigned config is Active at the end<br>of this period, it becomes the LastKnownGood. Note that if Spec.ConfigSource is<br>reset to nil (use local defaults), the LastKnownGood is also immediately reset to nil,<br>because the local default config is always assumed good.<br>You should not make assumptions about the node's method of determining config stability<br>and correctness, as this may change or become configurable in the future.<br>+optional|

In the presence of network partitions, this object may still<br>exist after this timestamp, until an administrator or automated process can determine the<br>resource is fully terminated.<br>If not set, graceful deletion of the object has not been requested.<br><br>Populated by the system when a graceful deletion is requested.<br>Read-only.<br>More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#metadata<br>+optional|

Name is primarily intended for creation idempotence and configuration<br>definition.<br>Cannot be updated.<br>More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names#names<br>+optional|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accessModes|[[v1.PersistentVolumeAccessMode](#schemav1.persistentvolumeaccessmode)]|false|none|accessModes contains the desired access modes the volume should have.<br>More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#access-modes-1<br>+optional<br>+listType=atomic|
|dataSource|object|false|none|dataSource field can be used to specify either:<br>* An existing VolumeSnapshot object (snapshot.storage.k8s.io/VolumeSnapshot)<br>* An existing PVC (PersistentVolumeClaim)<br>If the provisioner or an external controller can support the specified data source,<br>it will create a new volume based on the contents of the specified data source.<br>When the AnyVolumeDataSource feature gate is enabled, dataSource contents will be copied to dataSourceRef,<br>and dataSourceRef contents will be copied to dataSource when dataSourceRef.namespace is not specified.<br>If the namespace is specified, then dataSourceRef will not be copied to dataSource.<br>+optional|
|dataSourceRef|object|false|none|dataSourceRef specifies the object from which to populate the volume with data, if a non-empty<br>volume is desired. This may be any object from a non-empty API group (non<br>core object) or a PersistentVolumeClaim object.<br>When this field is specified, volume binding will only succeed if the type of<br>the specified object matches some installed volume populator or dynamic<br>provisioner.<br>This field will replace the functionality of the dataSource field and as such<br>if both fields are non-empty, they must have the same value. For backwards<br>compatibility, when namespace isn't specified in dataSourceRef,<br>both fields (dataSource and dataSourceRef) will be set to the same<br>value automatically if one of them is empty and the other is non-empty.<br>When namespace is specified in dataSourceRef,<br>dataSource isn't set to the same value and must be empty.<br>There are three important differences between dataSource and dataSourceRef:<br>* While dataSource only allows two specific types of objects, dataSourceRef<br>  allows any non-core object, as well as PersistentVolumeClaim objects.<br>* While dataSource ignores disallowed values (dropping them), dataSourceRef<br>  preserves all values, and generates an error if a disallowed value is<br>  specified.<br>* While dataSource only allows local objects, dataSourceRef allows objects<br>  in any namespaces.<br>(Beta) Using this field requires the AnyVolumeDataSource feature gate to be enabled.<br>(Alpha) Using the namespace field of dataSourceRef requires the CrossNamespaceVolumeDataSource feature gate to be enabled.<br>+optional|
|resources|object|false|none|resources represents the minimum resources the volume should have.<br>Users are allowed to specify resource requirements<br>that are lower than previous value but must still be higher than capacity recorded in the<br>status field of the claim.<br>More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#resources<br>+optional|
|selector|object|false|none|selector is a label query over volumes to consider for binding.<br>+optional|
|storageClassName|string|false|none|storageClassName is the name of the StorageClass required by the claim.<br>More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#class-1<br>+optional|
|volumeAttributesClassName|string|false|none|volumeAttributesClassName may be used to set the VolumeAttributesClass used by this claim.<br>If specified, the CSI driver will create or update the volume with the attributes defined<br>in the corresponding VolumeAttributesClass. This has a different purpose than storageClassName,<br>it can be changed after the claim is created. An empty string or nil value indicates that no<br>VolumeAttributesClass will be applied to the claim. If the claim enters an Infeasible error state,<br>this field can be reset to its previous value (including nil) to cancel the modification.<br>If the resource referred to by volumeAttributesClass does not exist, this PersistentVolumeClaim will be<br>set to a Pending state, as reflected by the modifyVolumeStatus field, until such as a resource<br>exists.<br>More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-attributes-classes/<br>+featureGate=VolumeAttributesClass<br>+optional|
|volumeMode|object|false|none|volumeMode defines what type of volume is required by the claim.<br>Value of Filesystem is implied when not included in claim spec.<br>+optional|
|volumeName|string|false|none|volumeName is the binding reference to the PersistentVolume backing this claim.<br>+optional|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|accessModes|ReadWriteOnce|
|accessModes|ReadOnlyMany|
|accessModes|ReadWriteMany|
|accessModes|ReadWriteOncePod|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution|[[v1.WeightedPodAffinityTerm](#schemav1.weightedpodaffinityterm)]|false|none|The scheduler will prefer to schedule pods to nodes that satisfy<br>the affinity expressions specified by this field, but it may choose<br>a node that violates one or more of the expressions. The node that is<br>most preferred is the one with the greatest sum of weights, i.e.<br>for each node that meets all of the scheduling requirements (resource<br>request, requiredDuringScheduling affinity expressions, etc.),<br>compute a sum by iterating through the elements of this field and adding<br>"weight" to the sum if the node has pods which matches the corresponding podAffinityTerm; the<br>node(s) with the highest sum are the most preferred.<br>+optional<br>+listType=atomic|
|requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution|[[v1.PodAffinityTerm](#schemav1.podaffinityterm)]|false|none|If the affinity requirements specified by this field are not met at<br>scheduling time, the pod will not be scheduled onto the node.<br>If the affinity requirements specified by this field cease to be met<br>at some point during pod execution (e.g. due to a pod label update), the<br>system may or may not try to eventually evict the pod from its node.<br>When there are multiple elements, the lists of nodes corresponding to each<br>podAffinityTerm are intersected, i.e. all terms must be satisfied.<br>+optional<br>+listType=atomic|

```json
{
  "labelSelector": {
    "matchExpressions": [
      {
        "key": "string",
        "operator": {},
        "values": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "matchLabels": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  },
  "matchLabelKeys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "mismatchLabelKeys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "namespaceSelector": {
    "matchExpressions": [
      {
        "key": "string",
        "operator": {},
        "values": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "matchLabels": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  },
  "namespaces": [
    "string"
  ],
  "topologyKey": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|labelSelector|object|false|none|A label query over a set of resources, in this case pods.<br>If it's null, this PodAffinityTerm matches with no Pods.<br>+optional|
|matchLabelKeys|[string]|false|none|MatchLabelKeys is a set of pod label keys to select which pods will<br>be taken into consideration. The keys are used to lookup values from the<br>incoming pod labels, those key-value labels are merged with `labelSelector` as `key in (value)`<br>to select the group of existing pods which pods will be taken into consideration<br>for the incoming pod's pod (anti) affinity. Keys that don't exist in the incoming<br>pod labels will be ignored. The default value is empty.<br>The same key is forbidden to exist in both matchLabelKeys and labelSelector.<br>Also, matchLabelKeys cannot be set when labelSelector isn't set.<br><br>+listType=atomic<br>+optional|
|mismatchLabelKeys|[string]|false|none|MismatchLabelKeys is a set of pod label keys to select which pods will<br>be taken into consideration. The keys are used to lookup values from the<br>incoming pod labels, those key-value labels are merged with `labelSelector` as `key notin (value)`<br>to select the group of existing pods which pods will be taken into consideration<br>for the incoming pod's pod (anti) affinity. Keys that don't exist in the incoming<br>pod labels will be ignored. The default value is empty.<br>The same key is forbidden to exist in both mismatchLabelKeys and labelSelector.<br>Also, mismatchLabelKeys cannot be set when labelSelector isn't set.<br><br>+listType=atomic<br>+optional|
|namespaceSelector|object|false|none|A label query over the set of namespaces that the term applies to.<br>The term is applied to the union of the namespaces selected by this field<br>and the ones listed in the namespaces field.<br>null selector and null or empty namespaces list means "this pod's namespace".<br>An empty selector ({}) matches all namespaces.<br>+optional|
|namespaces|[string]|false|none|namespaces specifies a static list of namespace names that the term applies to.<br>The term is applied to the union of the namespaces listed in this field<br>and the ones selected by namespaceSelector.<br>null or empty namespaces list and null namespaceSelector means "this pod's namespace".<br>+optional<br>+listType=atomic|
|topologyKey|string|false|none|This pod should be co-located (affinity) or not co-located (anti-affinity) with the pods matching<br>the labelSelector in the specified namespaces, where co-located is defined as running on a node<br>whose value of the label with key topologyKey matches that of any node on which any of the<br>selected pods is running.<br>Empty topologyKey is not allowed.|

|preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution|[[v1.WeightedPodAffinityTerm](#schemav1.weightedpodaffinityterm)]|false|none|The scheduler will prefer to schedule pods to nodes that satisfy<br>the anti-affinity expressions specified by this field, but it may choose<br>a node that violates one or more of the expressions. The node that is<br>most preferred is the one with the greatest sum of weights, i.e.<br>for each node that meets all of the scheduling requirements (resource<br>request, requiredDuringScheduling anti-affinity expressions, etc.),<br>compute a sum by iterating through the elements of this field and subtracting<br>"weight" from the sum if the node has pods which matches the corresponding podAffinityTerm; the<br>node(s) with the highest sum are the most preferred.<br>+optional<br>+listType=atomic|

<h2 id="tocS_v1.PodCertificateProjection">v1.PodCertificateProjection</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
{
  "certificateChainPath": "string",
  "credentialBundlePath": "string",
  "keyPath": "string",
  "keyType": "string",
  "maxExpirationSeconds": 0,
  "signerName": "string",
  "userAnnotations": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|certificateChainPath|string|false|none|Write the certificate chain at this path in the projected volume.<br><br>Most applications should use credentialBundlePath.  When using keyPath<br>and certificateChainPath, your application needs to check that the key<br>and leaf certificate are consistent, because it is possible to read the<br>files mid-rotation.<br><br>+optional|
|credentialBundlePath|string|false|none|Write the credential bundle at this path in the projected volume.<br><br>The credential bundle is a single file that contains multiple PEM blocks.<br>The first PEM block is a PRIVATE KEY block, containing a PKCS#8 private<br>key.<br><br>The remaining blocks are CERTIFICATE blocks, containing the issued<br>certificate chain from the signer (leaf and any intermediates).<br><br>Using credentialBundlePath lets your Pod's application code make a single<br>atomic read that retrieves a consistent key and certificate chain.  If you<br>project them to separate files, your application code will need to<br>additionally check that the leaf certificate was issued to the key.<br><br>+optional|
|keyPath|string|false|none|Write the key at this path in the projected volume.<br><br>Most applications should use credentialBundlePath.  When using keyPath<br>and certificateChainPath, your application needs to check that the key<br>and leaf certificate are consistent, because it is possible to read the<br>files mid-rotation.<br><br>+optional|
|keyType|string|false|none|The type of keypair Kubelet will generate for the pod.<br><br>Valid values are "RSA3072", "RSA4096", "ECDSAP256", "ECDSAP384",<br>"ECDSAP521", and "ED25519".<br><br>+required|
|maxExpirationSeconds|integer|false|none|maxExpirationSeconds is the maximum lifetime permitted for the<br>certificate.<br><br>Kubelet copies this value verbatim into the PodCertificateRequests it<br>generates for this projection.<br><br>If omitted, kube-apiserver will set it to 86400(24 hours). kube-apiserver<br>will reject values shorter than 3600 (1 hour).  The maximum allowable<br>value is 7862400 (91 days).<br><br>The signer implementation is then free to issue a certificate with any<br>lifetime *shorter* than MaxExpirationSeconds, but no shorter than 3600<br>seconds (1 hour).  This constraint is enforced by kube-apiserver.<br>`kubernetes.io` signers will never issue certificates with a lifetime<br>longer than 24 hours.<br><br>+optional|
|signerName|string|false|none|Kubelet's generated CSRs will be addressed to this signer.<br><br>+required|
|userAnnotations|object|false|none|userAnnotations allow pod authors to pass additional information to<br>the signer implementation.  Kubernetes does not restrict or validate this<br>metadata in any way.<br><br>These values are copied verbatim into the `spec.unverifiedUserAnnotations` field of<br>the PodCertificateRequest objects that Kubelet creates.<br><br>Entries are subject to the same validation as object metadata annotations,<br>with the addition that all keys must be domain-prefixed. No restrictions<br>are placed on values, except an overall size limitation on the entire field.<br><br>Signers should document the keys and values they support. Signers should<br>deny requests that contain keys they do not recognize.|

The permission bits are OR'd with rw-rw----<br><br>If unset, the Kubelet will not modify the ownership and permissions of any volume.<br>Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows.<br>+optional|
|fsGroupChangePolicy|object|false|none|fsGroupChangePolicy defines behavior of changing ownership and permission of the volume<br>before being exposed inside Pod. This field will only apply to<br>volume types which support fsGroup based ownership(and permissions).<br>It will have no effect on ephemeral volume types such as: secret, configmaps<br>and emptydir.<br>Valid values are "OnRootMismatch" and "Always". If not specified, "Always" is used.<br>Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows.<br>+optional|
|runAsGroup|integer|false|none|The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process.<br>Uses runtime default if unset.<br>May also be set in SecurityContext.  If set in both SecurityContext and<br>PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence<br>for that container.<br>Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows.<br>+optional|
|runAsNonRoot|boolean|false|none|Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user.<br>If true, the Kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it<br>does not run as UID 0 (root) and fail to start the container if it does.<br>If unset or false, no such validation will be performed.<br>May also be set in SecurityContext.  If set in both SecurityContext and<br>PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.<br>+optional|
|runAsUser|integer|false|none|The UID to run the entrypoint of the container process.<br>Defaults to user specified in image metadata if unspecified.<br>May also be set in SecurityContext.  If set in both SecurityContext and<br>PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence<br>for that container.<br>Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows.<br>+optional|
|seLinuxChangePolicy|object|false|none|seLinuxChangePolicy defines how the container's SELinux label is applied to all volumes used by the Pod.<br>It has no effect on nodes that do not support SELinux or to volumes does not support SELinux.<br>Valid values are "MountOption" and "Recursive".<br><br>"Recursive" means relabeling of all files on all Pod volumes by the container runtime.<br>This may be slow for large volumes, but allows mixing privileged and unprivileged Pods sharing the same volume on the same node.<br><br>"MountOption" mounts all eligible Pod volumes with `-o context` mount option.<br>This requires all Pods that share the same volume to use the same SELinux label.<br>It is not possible to share the same volume among privileged and unprivileged Pods.<br>Eligible volumes are in-tree FibreChannel and iSCSI volumes, and all CSI volumes<br>whose CSI driver announces SELinux support by setting spec.seLinuxMount: true in their<br>CSIDriver instance. Other volumes are always re-labelled recursively.<br>"MountOption" value is allowed only when SELinuxMount feature gate is enabled.<br><br>If not specified and SELinuxMount feature gate is enabled, "MountOption" is used.<br>If not specified and SELinuxMount feature gate is disabled, "MountOption" is used for ReadWriteOncePod volumes<br>and "Recursive" for all other volumes.<br><br>This field affects only Pods that have SELinux label set, either in PodSecurityContext or in SecurityContext of all containers.<br><br>All Pods that use the same volume should use the same seLinuxChangePolicy, otherwise some pods can get stuck in ContainerCreating state.<br>Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows.<br>+featureGate=SELinuxChangePolicy<br>+optional|
|seLinuxOptions|object|false|none|The SELinux context to be applied to all containers.<br>If unspecified, the container runtime will allocate a random SELinux context for each<br>container.  May also be set in SecurityContext.  If set in<br>both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext<br>takes precedence for that container.<br>Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows.<br>+optional|
|seccompProfile|object|false|none|The seccomp options to use by the containers in this pod.<br>Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows.<br>+optional|
|supplementalGroups|[integer]|false|none|A list of groups applied to the first process run in each container, in<br>addition to the container's primary GID and fsGroup (if specified).  If<br>the SupplementalGroupsPolicy feature is enabled, the<br>supplementalGroupsPolicy field determines whether these are in addition<br>to or instead of any group memberships defined in the container image.<br>If unspecified, no additional groups are added, though group memberships<br>defined in the container image may still be used, depending on the<br>supplementalGroupsPolicy field.<br>Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows.<br>+optional<br>+listType=atomic|
|supplementalGroupsPolicy|object|false|none|Defines how supplemental groups of the first container processes are calculated.<br>Valid values are "Merge" and "Strict". If not specified, "Merge" is used.<br>(Alpha) Using the field requires the SupplementalGroupsPolicy feature gate to be enabled<br>and the container runtime must implement support for this feature.<br>Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows.<br>TODO: update the default value to "Merge" when spec.os.name is not windows in v1.34<br>+featureGate=SupplementalGroupsPolicy<br>+optional|
|sysctls|[[v1.Sysctl](#schemav1.sysctl)]|false|none|Sysctls hold a list of namespaced sysctls used for the pod. Pods with unsupported<br>sysctls (by the container runtime) might fail to launch.<br>Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows.<br>+optional<br>+listType=atomic|
|windowsOptions|object|false|none|The Windows specific settings applied to all containers.<br>If unspecified, the options within a container's SecurityContext will be used.<br>If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.<br>Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is linux.<br>+optional|
